1.text: There was a certain man from the tribe of Benjamin, whose name was called Maqabis.

2.text: He had three sons, fair of countenance and exceedingly strong; and they were beloved by every people throughout the dominion of Ṣiruṣaydan — in the land of the Chaldeans, in Midian, and in the country of the Medes.

3.text: When [the king’s officers] found them, they said to them: “As the king has commanded, will you not bow down to the gods of Ṣiruṣaydan? Will you not offer sacrifice?

4.text: And if you refuse, we will seize you and bring you before the king; and as the king has commanded, we will destroy all your possessions.”

5.text: Those handsome young men answered them: “We have the God of our fathers, to whom we bow down — He who created heaven and earth, the sea and what is in it, the sun and the moon, the stars and the clouds. He is the true God whom we worship and in whom we trust.”

6.text: Those officers of the king were four commanders, and the attendants who bore their arms were fifty for each one.

7.text: When they wished to seize these holy ones, [the brothers] escaped from their hands, and none could touch them. For those young men were warriors of utterly overpowering strength; they took up shield and spear and went forth.

8.text: Among them was one who would strangle a bear and kill it — he would choke it like a chicken on the spot.

9.text: Among them was one who would kill a lion with a single stone, or with a single blow of a staff.

10.text: Among them was one who in time of battle, with one stroke of a single sword, would kill a man at once; and so their name and their renown were proclaimed throughout all the land of Moab and of the Chaldeans.

11.text: They were warriors of great strength; and they had comeliness, and the loveliness of speech.

12.text: Moreover, the beauty of their outward appearance was wonderful; but because they worshiped God and did not fear death, the beauty of their inward heart surpassed all.

13.text: When they had terrified the troops, none was able to seize them; being mighty, they went up to a high mountain and escaped.

14.text: Then those troops returned to the city and shut the gate of the fortress; and they terrified the people, saying: “Unless you bring us those warriors — the Meqabyans — we will burn your city with fire, and we will send word to the king and lay waste your country.”

15.text: Then the people of the country — the poor and the rich, men and women, the orphan whose father and mother had died, and the widows — all came out and cried out together. They turned their eyes toward the mountain and cried out to them: “Do not destroy us and our country!”

16.text: And at that time they wept together; and because of God, they were afraid.

17.text: They turned their faces toward the east, and stretching out their hands, they prayed together to God, saying: “O Lord, shall we say ‘No’ to these men who have broken your commandment and your law?

18.text: “As for us, we have no desire to hear the word of that lawless man who does not believe in your law but trusts in gold and silver, and in stone and wood made by the hand of man.

19.text: “While You are the Creator who saves and who kills, he makes himself as though they [the idols] had created him; he is one who sheds the blood of man and eats the flesh of man.

20.text: “As for us, we have no desire to see that lawless man’s face or to hear his speech.

21.text: “But if You command us, we will go to him; because we have trusted in You, we will hand over our bodies to death; and when he commands, ‘Sacrifice to the gods,’ we will not hearken to the word of that lawless man.

22.text: “O Lord, God of our fathers — who did Your will and remained steadfast in Your law — You who search the kidneys and the heart, God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob: as for us, we have trusted in You with our whole heart.

23.text: “You search the heart of man and discern both the sinner and the righteous; nothing is hidden from You; what is concealed is revealed before You.

24.text: “As for us, we have no other God besides You.

25.text: “But for the sake of Your holy name — that we may give our bodies over to death — be for us, in this work in which we submit ourselves to You, strength, firmness, and refuge.

26.text: “When Israel went down into the land of Egypt, You heard the prayer of Jacob; now also, O Holy God, we entreat You.”

27.text: When their appearance was utterly resplendent, and the two parties stood face to face and beheld one another, swords of fire descended like terrifying lightning; and in that moment they [the swords] cut their necks and slew them. And at that same moment they rose up alive as before.

28.text: The beauty of their appearance became utterly glorious; they shone more brightly than the sun; they became more lovely than before.

1.text: And there came a voice from heaven, saying: “Servants of God Most High — Abya, Sila, Fentos! As you have seen these who died and rose again before your eyes, so also after your own death shall you rise; and your faces shall shine in the kingdom of heaven.

2.text: “Go with those men, and there receive your martyrdom.”

3.text: Then they prayed and gave thanks, and bowed down to God; neither death nor the punishments of the king terrified them.

4.text: And they went to those officers; they were like a lamb without malice and offered them no fight. When they reached them, the officers seized them and beat them; they bound them and scourged them, and brought them before the king and made them stand in his presence.

5.text: And the king answered them: “You rebels — how is it that you will not sacrifice to the gods? How is it that you will not bow down?”

6.text: Those holy and blessed ones, the elect and joyful, the wonder-precious-as-jewels brothers Abya, Sila, and Fentos answered him with one voice.

7.text: They said to that pestilent king: “As for us, we will not sacrifice to defiled idols which have neither knowledge nor understanding; nor will we bow down to them.

8.text: “Further: we will not bow down to idols which are the work of human hands — gold and silver, stone and wood — which have neither soul nor mind nor knowledge, which do no good to those who do good to them, and do no evil to those who do evil to them.”

9.text: And the king answered: “Why do you do this? They know those who slander them and wrong them — why do you slander the honorable gods?”

10.text: They answered: “Because in our sight they are as nothing — therefore we slander them; and we will not honor them.”

11.text: And the king said: “According to the measure of the wickedness of your deeds I will punish you; with grievous torment and with scourges, and with fire I will destroy the comeliness of your appearance.

12.text: “Now then — tell me whether you will sacrifice to the gods or whether you will not; and if not, I will raise scourging and sword against you.”

13.text: They answered: “As for us, we will not sacrifice to defiled idols; nor will we bow down.” And the king commanded that they be beaten with thick rods, then scourged with whips, and after that flayed until their inward parts were visible.

14.text: After this he commanded that they be bound and shut up in prison, until he should take counsel how to punish them and put them to death.

15.text: And they took them and, without pity, bound them in prison with strong bonds; and they remained in prison three days and three nights.

16.text: After three days the king commanded the crier to go about summoning his nobles and counselors, his officers, and the elders of the country to assemble.

17.text: And when King Ṣiruṣaydan was seated in the public square, he commanded that those honorable ones — Abya, Sila, and Fentos — be brought; bound and wounded, they stood before him.

18.text: And the king said: “In these three days of your sitting, have you turned with a turning of repentance? Or do you remain in your former wickedness?”

19.text: Those honorable soldiers of God answered: “As for us, we are resolute. We will never consent to worship an idol full of sin and wickedness, such as you yourself worship.”

20.text: Then that criminal, in his anger, commanded that they be hung up and that their wounds be reopened; and their blood ran upon the ground.

21.text: Again he commanded that they be burned with torches and that their flesh be roasted; and they did so. And those honorable men said to him: “You godless one — speak on! According to the measure by which you multiply our punishment, our reward is multiplied.”

22.text: Again he commanded that ravening beasts — leopard and bear and lion — be brought, having been kept from their food, that they might wholly consume their flesh with their bones.

23.text: And he commanded the beast-keepers to set the beasts upon them; they did as he commanded. They bound the holy martyrs limb to limb; and again, with cunning, they drove stakes through and pinned them.

24.text: But the beasts came roaring and were unleashed upon them; and when they reached the martyrs, they bowed down to them and paid them homage.

25.text: Roaring, they turned back upon their keepers; they terrified the keepers and pursued them until they brought them all the way to the king’s presence.

26.text: And there they killed seventy-five men from among the soldiers of the criminals.

27.text: With terror, the people crowded one upon another and many were crushed, until the king left his throne and fled. And with great difficulty they seized the beasts and brought them back to their lair.

28.text: Then came the two brothers of Abya, Sila, and Fentos; and loosing them from the bonds with which they were bound, they said to them: “Come, let us flee, lest these criminals and waverers find us.”

29.text: Those martyrs answered their brothers: “After we have stood for martyrdom it is not fitting that we flee. If you yourselves are afraid, flee and go.”

30.text: And those, their younger brothers, said: “We also will stand with you before the king; if you die, we will die with you.”

31.text: After this, the king on the gallery above the hall of his kingdom saw that those blessed men had been loosed and that all five brothers stood together. The officers who marshaled and punished the troops, having inquired and learned that they were brothers, reported it to the king; and the king, in his anger, roared like a wild boar in the wilderness.

32.text: And the king commanded that all five brothers together be seized and cast into prison until he should take counsel how to punish them. With unhewn timber he had them bound with grievous bonds, and they laid them in prison.

33.text: And King Ṣiruṣaydan said: “These wandering young men have wearied me. How firm is the mind of these men! And the wickedness of their work is as the firmness of their strength; whenever I think they will turn, they make their minds the worse for it.

34.text: “I will repay them according to the measure of their wicked work. I will burn their flesh with fire until they are charred ash; and I will scatter the ash of their flesh on a mountain like dust, so that the wind may carry them away.”

35.text: When he had said this, after three days he commanded that those holy ones be brought; and when those holy ones drew near, in a great pit-furnace he commanded that fire be kindled, and that they cast into it the things that should make the fire rage and the cauldron boil — pitch and tow, sea-foam and resin, and brimstone.

36.text: When the fire in the pit was blazing, the messengers came to the king saying: “We have done what you commanded; send the man who is to be added to it.”

37.text: And he commanded that they be received and cast into the fire-pit. The officers did as the king commanded; and as those holy ones entered into the fire, they gave their souls to God.

38.text: And angels received them — the very men who had cast them in seeing it. Their souls they took to where Abraham and Isaac and Jacob are — to Paradise where joy is found.

1.text: When that criminal saw that they were dead, he commanded that their flesh be burned with fire until they became ash, and that the wind scatter them. But the fire was unable to burn even the hair of their heads from the body; and they took them out of the pit.

2.text: Again, from morning till evening, they kindled fire over them; it did not touch them. They said: “Now then, come — let us cast their corpses into the sea.”

3.text: The king commanded as they had said, and they cast them into the sea. Heavy iron weights and great stones, and a millstone such as a donkey turns by the wheel — they added these and cast them with them; but the sea did not drown them. The Spirit of God was upon them, and they floated on the sea and did not sink into its deep; and in all the cunning that was contrived against them, they could not be destroyed.

4.text: And he said: “Their death has wearied me more than their life. What shall I do but throw their corpses to the wild beasts, that they may eat them?”

5.text: They did so; but the beasts and the carrion-birds did not touch their corpses. Carrion-birds and birds of the air covered them with their wings, that the sun might not burn them; and the corpses of those five martyrs remained for fourteen days.

6.text: When the people saw them, their bodies shone like the rays of the sun. And so that light might encompass them as a tent, angels surrounded their corpses.

7.text: He took counsel and found nothing he could do; after this, he dug into the earth and buried the corpses of the five martyrs.

8.text: And to that godless king as he lay sleeping on his bed by night, the five martyrs appeared in his presence, drawing their swords and standing in his face by night.

9.text: When he woke from his sleep, fearing — it seemed to him that they had entered his house by criminal means — he desired to flee from corner to corner of the house. It seemed to him that they had laid charges against him, and that they would kill him; and out of fear his knees trembled.

10.text: Therefore he said: “Lords, what do you seek? What shall I do for you?”

11.text: They answered: “Are you not he who killed us by burning us in the fire, and who commanded us to be cast into the sea? Because we believed in God, he kept our bodies, and you were unable to destroy us. No one who believes in him perishes; therefore let praise and thanksgiving go up to God for his glory. We who believed in him were not put to shame in our affliction.”

12.text: “I did not know,” he said, “that such a punishment would overtake me; for the evil I have done against you — what payment shall I give you?

13.text: “Now then — determine for me the payment I shall give you, that you may not take my body in death, nor lead me down to Sheol while I am yet living.

14.text: “For I have transgressed against you; and because the law of God your father is merciful, forgive me my sin.”

15.text: Those blessed martyrs answered him: “We will repay you no evil for the evil you have done to us; the one who repays the wages is God — and our Creator God shall pay you your wages.

16.text: “But because of the smallness of your knowledge and the dullness of your mind, we have revealed ourselves to you, that you might see we are living; and we have prepared life for the one whom you thought you had killed.

17.text: “As for you and your idols’ priests — you shall descend to Gehenna whence there is no way out forever.

18.text: “You who, being a man of spittle, have abandoned bowing down to God who created you, and bow down to idols you yourselves worship — woe to those idols and to you! You do not know whence you have come; are you not vapor that appears today and tomorrow is gone?”

19.text: And the king answered: “What do you command me to do, that I may do all that you desire?”

20.text: “What we teach you is for your own sake, that you may not enter into the gehenna of fire; not for ours.

21.text: “For your idols are gold and silver, stone and wood, made by human hands; they have neither soul, nor mind, nor knowledge.

22.text: “They neither kill nor save; they do no good and no evil; they do not humble and do not honor; they do not impoverish and do not enrich; they do not uproot and do not plant.

23.text: “But by the spirit of demons who love that not even one of those whose hearts are blind, like yours, should be saved, they deceive you. While you are the ones who made them, it seems to you that they have made you.

24.text: “The spirits of demons and of Satan dwell in them; and as you have desired, they answer you back, to drown you in the sea of Gehenna.

25.text: “As for you — leave this error of yours and worship the Lord our God; let this be the wage we receive in place of our death, that we may profit our souls.”

26.text: And he stood astonished, marveling utterly. For all five had appeared to him with drawn swords, and he was afraid; therefore he bowed down to them.

27.text: “Now then,” he said, “I have known that the dust-dead in truth rise up after their death; and I myself had little remaining before dying.”

28.text: After this, the martyrs vanished from the king’s sight. And from that day onward, that Ṣiruṣaydan — utterly arrogant and proud — left off burning their corpses.

29.text: But after many days he became proud again in his idols, in the error of his mind, and was glad in them. It was not he alone who erred: until they should leave off following him, he led many like himself astray.

30.text: They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons; the desire of their mind which Satan their father had taught them — uproar and licentiousness, and that which God does not love — these they did. Fornication and licentiousness they wrought.

31.text: They married their own mothers; they defiled their sisters and aunts; this defiling work and everything that resembled it they did; their bodies they defiled. Satan had hardened the minds of those perverted people, and they said: “We will not turn back.”

32.text: That Ṣiruṣaydan, ignorant of his Creator, was proud and arrogant, and put his trust in his idols.

33.text: “How,” he said, “shall God give kingship to those who do not know him? It is because he tests them, that they may utterly return to him.”

34.text: But if they had utterly returned, he would have loved them and preserved their kingdom; but since they refused, he will punish them in the writhing of Gehenna forever.

35.text: A king, then, in proportion to the greatness of his kingship, ought to fear the Lord God; and as a judge, in proportion to the greatness of his dominion, ought to submit himself in goodness to his Creator.

36.text: The great elders, the chiefs, and the officers also, in proportion to the greatness of their honor, ought to obey their Creator.

37.text: For he is Lord of heaven and earth, who created all his creation; he is the one who impoverishes and the one who enriches, who humbles and who honors; for above in heaven and below on earth, there is no other God besides him.

1.text: Re’aytawi boasted; but God, by a single mosquito-bite, made his body swell from foot to head; and by that little mosquito he died.

2.text: Again, Nimrod boasted, who because of the abundance of his violence had a bed of iron made for himself; and God destroyed him.

3.text: Again, Nebuchadnezzar boasted: “There is no king besides me; I am the one who makes the sun rise upon the earth.” So he spoke from the abundance of his arrogance.

4.text: God separated him from humankind and sent him into the wilderness for seven years; he made his lot with the beasts of the wilderness and the birds of heaven, until he should know that the one who made him is God.

5.text: And when he knew, God restored him again to his kingdom. Who has boasted with arrogance against God his Creator, and the earth has not also become his ash?

6.text: Who has broken his law and his ordinance, and the earth has not swallowed him?

7.text: “Ṣiruṣaydan, you also desire to boast against your Creator; he also shall destroy you because of your arrogance, as he did them, and bring you down to the grave.

8.text: “Furthermore, he shall bring you down to Sheol — the end of darkness, where there is gnashing of teeth and weeping; and after you have entered, to the great and deep pit from which there is no exit forever.

9.text: “For you yourself are tomorrow’s mortal and shall perish, like the arrogant kings who were as you and have left this world’s life.”

10.text: As for us, we say: “You are a man and not God. The God who made earth and heaven also made you;

11.text: “and he it is who brings down the proud, and who honors the humble; who gives strength to the weary, and gives weariness to the strong.

12.text: “He kills the living, and again raises the dead who have been buried in the grave and have become dust.

13.text: “And he frees slaves from the bondage of sin into life.

14.text: “O King Ṣiruṣaydan! Why do you boast in your defiled idols, which are of no profit?

15.text: “For God it was who created the heavens, who founded the earth, who made the great sea, who made the sun and the moon, who established times and years.

16.text: “A man goes out to his tilling and remains plowing until dusk; and the stars of heaven endure standing fast by his word.

17.text: “He calls them all by their names; and there is no thing that comes to be without God knowing it.

18.text: “He commanded the angels of heaven that they should serve him and praise his honored name; and the angels are sent to all those who shall inherit life.

19.text: “The angel Raphael was sent to Tobit; and he saved Tobiah in the land of Raguel.

20.text: “An angel was sent to Gideon, that he might make known to him how to destroy the Ammonites; and an angel was sent to the prophet Moses when Israel crossed the Red Sea.

21.text: “For thus it is written: ‘God alone led them, and there was no other god with them.’ [Deut 32:12]

22.text: “He brought them to the harvest that is upon the earth.

23.text: “He fed them with the grain of the threshing-floor; he loved them utterly, and fed them with honey from the rock. [Deut 32:13]

24.text: “He made you king over the people; he gave you authority over the four kingdoms, that you might keep his people faithfully and do the will of God your Creator.

25.text: “He set you above all in kingship, that you might love your Creator God in full.

26.text: “And you, as you have loved him and trusted him over all his people — you ought to love God your Creator utterly, and do God’s will, that your days upon all the earth may be multiplied, and that he may dwell with you,

27.text: “and stand up for you against your enemies, and seat you upon all your thrones, and shelter you with his wing.

28.text: “For if you should know — when God chose Saul from among the sons of Israel and made him king over his people Israel, while he was tending his father’s donkeys, and seated him on the throne with the prophet Samuel — so also has he chosen you.

29.text: “He separated him from his brothers and gave him a high lot, saying: ’From this day God makes you king over the people Israel, that you may keep his people;

30.text: “that you may kill and save, since God has appointed you over them; keep with good those who do good and with evil those who do evil.

31.text: “For though you scourge or save, that you may do his will, God has appointed you over all. Repay the doers of good with good; and the doers of evil with evil.

32.text: “You are the servant of God who rules all in heaven; in everything you have planned, submitting yourself before him — that he may do your will in everything you have asked — you also, in every time and every hour, do the will of God.

33.text: “For there is none who rules him; but he rules all.

34.text: “There is none who appoints him; but he appoints all.

35.text: “There is none who removes him; but he removes all.

36.text: “There is none who blames him; but he blames all.

37.text: “There is none who summons him; but he summons all. The authority of heaven and earth is his; there is none who escapes his hand; before him all is revealed, and there is nothing hidden from his eye.

38.text: “He sees all; but there is none who sees him. He hears the prayer of those who pray to him; he receives their prayer; for he created humankind in his image and in his likeness.

39.text: “And from his treasury that does not fail, he feeds all. For he is King who endures forever.”

1.text: “For he truly makes king those kings who do his will; and the kings have written what is straight concerning him.

2.text: “Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, David and Solomon and Hezekiah, and all the holy kings whose dwelling is light — he shines upon their dwelling with light that cannot be searched out.

3.text: “Not as the hall that is upon earth; but the hall that is in heaven, utterly luminous. Its floor of gold and silver and pearl is pure.

4.text: “Its utterly shining appearance is removed from the mind of man. The hall of the kingdom of heaven shines with topaz and emerald, with chalcedony and aquamarine.

5.text: “It is a kingdom-hall shining utterly with precious gems beyond man’s imagining. It is the hall of the kingdom of heaven that he himself, God, has fashioned as he knows it. Its floor is of gold and silver, of sky-blue gem and green gem, of yellow gem, and the color of white silk — pure.

6.text: “Thus it is utterly beautiful — pure and luminous.

7.text: “It is built with righteousness and truth; and made with forgiveness and mercy.

8.text: “And from it flows water of life, whiter than the sun; there is a tent of light, fragranced with the perfume of Hermon.

9.text: “And around its house, sweet fruit of Paradise is planted, whose form and scent are surpassing. And there is a place of vine and olive — utterly beautiful, of pleasing fragrance.

10.text: “If a fleshly man should enter it, from the sweetness of its scent and the abundance of its joy his soul would be parted from his flesh.

11.text: “And in it those good kings who did the will of God are made glad; their work and their place are known in the kingdom of heaven, in the place of eternal life.

12.text: “As the glory of their kingship was on earth, so is it in heaven; just as they were honored on earth and bowed down to, so are they honored in heaven; and they are exalted. Even in this world they are made glad if they do good work.

13.text: “But wicked kings — who do not judge truly and rightly in the kingship and dominion God has given them, who have neglected the cry of the poor and of those who fast for lack of food, who do not save the oppressed and the foreigner and the orphan;

14.text: “who do not deliver the poor and the hungry from those who plunder them; who do not satisfy the hungry from their food; who do not give drink to the thirsty from their drink; who have not turned their ear to the cry of the poor —

15.text: “these shall be brought down to the dwelling of Sheol, which is the end of darkness; and as David said in his psalm — ‘Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, and do not chastise me in your wrath’ [Ps. 6:1] — when that great day God has prepared, and his wrath, comes upon them, according to the abundance of their renown so shall their hardship and shame abound.

16.text: “While kings and princes upon earth rule this world, they take those who have not kept his law.

17.text: “But in heaven there is God who rules all; the soul of all is in his hand; the life of all is in his mouth; he it is who gives honor to those who honor him; he is all-powerful; he rules all and loves those who love him.

18.text: “He, the King of heaven and earth, searches heart and kidneys; he gives the wages of his prayer to whoever has prayed to him with a pure heart.

19.text: “He shall destroy the arrogance of the mighty who do evil to widows and orphans.

20.text: “It was not by your strength that you took hold of this kingdom; it was not by your competence that you have sat upon this throne. But God, having permitted that you be tested as Saul was tested — Saul who, in his days, in ruling his people, despised the word of God and the word of Samuel, and did not kill the king of Amalek and his army — set you on the throne of the kingdom.

21.text: “For God had told the prophet Samuel: ‘Go, say to Saul: They have grieved me by breaking the law and worshiping their idols, and by bowing to the idol in its sanctuaries, and in all their worthless defiled work — therefore, go to the country of Amalek; from man to beast, kings and their armies — all, destroy.’

22.text: “Therefore, when they had grieved God, he sent him to destroy them.

23.text: “But Saul saved their king; many cattle, and women and virgins; and from among the young men, the handsome ones — he saved. Therefore God said to the prophet Samuel: ’He has set my word at nothing; he has not obeyed my commandment; go and divide his kingship from him.

24.text: “In his place, anoint David the son of Jesse to reign over Israel.

25.text: “And in him [in Saul] let a demon that grips and casts him down be set to work.

26.text: “He whom I had given the kingdom that he might do my will has refused; and when he refused to do my will, I removed him from his honor. But you — go, tell him; say thus to him: As for God who set you king over his people Israel, and who seated you on the throne of the kingdom — do you thus despise him?

27.text: “You have not known the God who gave you such great honor and renown.’”

28.text: “And the prophet Samuel went to King Saul. He went in to him while he was seated at table, with Agag king of Amalek seated at his left.

29.text: “‘Why have you utterly despised God,’ he said, ‘who commanded you to destroy man and beast?’

30.text: “At that time, the king arose in fear from his throne, and laid hold of Samuel’s garment; but Samuel refused to turn back, and Samuel’s garment was rent.

31.text: “And Samuel said to Saul: ‘God has divided your kingdom.’

32.text: “Again Saul said to Samuel: ‘Honor me before the people, and make atonement for my sin before God, that he may forgive me.’ But Samuel refused to alter the word — for he feared the word of his Creator God, and did not fear a mortal king.

33.text: “Therefore, that he might not swallow what he had not chewed, he ran through Agag king of Amalek.”

34.text: “And as for that godless one who had broken God’s word, an unclean spirit took him; it struck him in the head. For God does not stand in awe of a king who does iniquity; he is the King of kings who commands all.

35.text: “For he is Lord of all his creation, who removes the rule of every king and prince whom they do not fear; there is none who commands him.

36.text: “As it has been said: ‘The house of David goes growing ever more great; but the house of Saul goes ever more low’ [2 Sam 3:1] — so he destroyed the kingdom from Saul and his son.

37.text: “Because he was grieved, and because he had not destroyed the criminals who had grieved him by their evil work, God in his vengeance destroyed the house of Saul. For the one who does not avenge the enemy of God is himself the enemy of God.

38.text: “He who can avenge, and to whom authority has been given, but who does not avenge the sinner — the one who avenges not him who has no law of God — that man is in truth the enemy of God.”

1.text: “You also, whether king or governor — what are you? Is it not God who created you?

2.text: “He brought you from non-existence into existence, that you might do his will, walk in his commandment, and fear his judgment. Just as you are angry with your slaves and rule over them, so also is there one who is angry with you and rules over you.

3.text: “As you strike sinners without mercy, so also is there God who strikes you, and who shall add to you a judgment which has no end forever.

4.text: “As you scourge whoever has not submitted to you and not brought a tribute-gift, why do you not bring a tribute-gift to God?

5.text: “As you wish to be feared, why do you not fear God your Creator? For it is he who created you and made you king over all his creation, that you might faithfully keep his people and his flock.

6.text: “Judge truly and rightly as God has appointed you; do not show favor to great or small. Whom shall you fear, except him? Keep his way and his commandment.

7.text: “As Moses commanded the sons of Israel: ‘I have set before you fire and water; stretch out your hand to whichever you have chosen’ [cf. Sir 15:16] — do not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.

8.text: “So that you may hear his word and do his commandment, hear the word I tell you: that you might not say, ‘Across the sea, across the deep, across the river — there is the word; who will bring it to me that I may see, that I may hear the word, that I may do God’s commandment?’

9.text: “And again that you might not say: ‘Who will go up to heaven for me and bring down for me that word of God, that I may hear and do it?’ Behold, the word is near in your mouth; it is in your hand. [Deut 30:11–14]

10.text: “If you have not heard the book, you have not heard God your Creator; if you have not kept his word, you have not loved him; you have not done his commandment.

11.text: “And you, if you have not loved his commandment and not done the will of him who set you apart from all your kindred and honored you and made you great — you shall enter judgment forever.

12.text: “He made you head and chief over all the people, that you might remember the name of God your Creator; he gave you to rule his people truly and rightly.

13.text: “There are those whom you punish among the people who have transgressed against you; there is also one whom you forgive, having remembered God’s way and inclining your heart in good and righteous judgment.

14.text: “When men plead before you, do not show partiality; the whole earth is your possession; do not take a bribe by which you might forgive the sinner and oppress the innocent.

15.text: “If you do his will, he will multiply your days upon the earth; but if you grieve him, he will diminish your days.

16.text: “Remember that you will rise from death, that whether good or evil — in all the work you have done — you shall stand before him to be examined.

17.text: “If you do good work, you shall dwell in the dwellings of the good kings, in houses of light. But if you do evil work, you shall dwell in the dwellings of the evil kings.

18.text: “God does not stand in awe of your kingly power. But you — when you have seen the splendor of your fearfulness, the trophies of your warriors, your hung-up war-armor; when you have seen your horses, the soldiers under your authority, those who blow trumpets and play harps before you —

19.text: “when you have seen all this, you exalt your understanding; you stiffen your neck; you forget him who has given you all this honor. When he says ‘Stop,’ are you not the one who must stop?

20.text: “He gave you the post you hold; and when you have utterly disregarded it, he gives your honor to another.

21.text: “For death will come on you suddenly, and at the resurrection judgment will be made, and every work of man will be examined; and there you shall be examined; he shall control you; he shall judge you.

22.text: “The kings of the earth have none to honor them in that day, since he is the Judge of truth; and at the time of judgment poor and rich shall stand together. The crowns in which the princes of the earth trust shall fall.

23.text: “Judgment is prepared; the soul trembles; the books are opened; the works of men are revealed; and there is none hidden.

24.text: “As when a woman comes to give birth, and the fetus within her womb has come to be born, the womb cannot keep it back — so shall the earth, at the time of the resurrection of the dead, return the trust deposited in it.

25.text: “Or — can the clouds keep back the rain so that they do not rain upon the place where God has commanded them? In the same way, since the word of God brought all from non-existence into existence and made it; and again, since the word of God has brought all into the grave — when the time of resurrection has come, it is not possible to make the dead not rise.

26.text: “Again, as he spoke to Moses: ‘Man does not live by bread alone, but by the word that comes from the mouth of God’ [Deut 8:3; Matt 4:4] — the word of God shall raise every man from the grave.

27.text: “Behold, it has been made known that the dead live by the word of God.

28.text: “Furthermore, concerning kings and princes and those who do his will, God said in Deuteronomy: ‘Their day of accounting has come; at the time of judgment, when their foot stumbles, I will avenge them’ [cf. Deut 32:35].

29.text: “Again, to those who do not know God’s judgment, God said: ’Know that I am God; I kill, and I save.

30.text: “‘I scourge, and I forgive; I lead down to Sheol and again I bring up to heaven; and there is none who escapes my hand.’ [Deut 32:39]

31.text: “To kings and princes who have not kept his law, God said: ’Earthly kingship passes away; from morning till evening it passes. Keep my law and my ordinance, that you may enter into my eternal kingdom.

32.text: “For the calling of God is for honor or for shame; this he humbles, and this he honors.

33.text: “Whoever has not done his will, he removes; and whoever has done his will, he appoints.’”

1.text: “Now hear also concerning the resurrection of the dead; let me tell you. Trees are planted; they put forth branches; the vine puts forth tendrils; and they make wine from it — for God brings forth its fruit from non-existence.

2.text: “Just look: that tree you planted was once small. But today it has put forth ends, leaf, and fruit.

3.text: “And God waters its root from two breasts — from water and from earth.

4.text: “But its wood he feeds from wind and from sun; the root waters the leaf with water; the earth gives firmness to the wood.

5.text: “And the wind which God created gives fruit in their midst. So also is the resurrection of the dead.

6.text: “When the soul has been separated from the flesh, having taken its course, God said: ‘Gather souls from the four corners — from water and earth, from fire and wind.’

7.text: “The nature of earth stood firm in itself; it became ash. The nature of water stood firm in itself; it became dew.

8.text: “The nature of wind stood firm in itself; it became wind. The nature of fire stood firm in itself; it became fire that gives warmth.

9.text: “But the soul God created returned to the hand of its Creator; when he wills, he restores it, and dwells it where he wills.

10.text: “The souls of the righteous he keeps in a house of light; the souls of sinners he keeps in a house of darkness, until the time he wills to bring them forth.

11.text: “To the prophet Ezekiel he said: ‘Call from the four corners that they may be gathered and may become one body.’ [Ezek 37:9]

12.text: “And when he had spoken thus with one word, they were gathered from the four corners.

13.text: “And the nature of water brought dew; again, the nature of fire brought warmth.

14.text: “The nature of earth again brought earth; the nature of wind brought breath.

15.text: “And God brought the soul from its dwelling where he had set it; in one word they were gathered, and the resurrection took place.

16.text: “And in your own experience, I will show you another sign: day darkens; you sleep; the night brightens; and you rise from your sleep. While you slept, you were of death.

17.text: “And when you woke, that is a sign of the resurrection. But the night, all darkness — that is a sign of this world. The whole world sleeps in it, for the darkness of night has covered them.

18.text: “But the morning light, in which darkness is taken away, by which there is light in all the world, by which a man rises and goes out to his work — that is a sign of the resurrection of the dead.

19.text: “This renewal of the world and the resurrection of the dead is thus; for this world passes away in the likeness of this night.

20.text: “And David said: ‘He has set its sign in the sun.’ [Ps. 19:4] When the sun rises and shines, it is the sign of this world.

21.text: “As the sun shines on this world today, so when he comes — even God himself — he will shine for the renewed world; he will shine as the sun. For he has said: ‘I am the sun that does not set, the lantern that does not fail’ [cf. Isa 60:19–20]; for God himself is its light.

22.text: “Furthermore, he will raise up the dead in the blink of an eye. And I will bring you another sign — from the food from which you sow, and by which you live: be it a kernel of wheat, of barley, or of lentil — there is no fruit-of-labor a man sows in the earth which sprouts unless it has first been undone.

23.text: “As you see, when all human flesh undergoes its undoing, the fruit with its chaff is consumed in the earth.

24.text: “And when the fruit is consumed, sprouting as a seventh part of the seed, God gives the breath of life as he wills; the root sprouts within the earth; and it puts forth leaf upon the earth.

25.text: “Just look: until it has been undone, it cannot sprout. But after it sprouts, it puts forth many shoots.

26.text: “To that shoot which has grown, fruit is given by God; and the fruit is enwrapped by the chaff.

27.text: “See only how the seed you have sown has multiplied; the leaf, the stalk, the chaff, and the head — they cannot be counted for you.

28.text: “Do not be foolish; see how your seed has multiplied; and even so think about the resurrection of the dead, and how each shall be repaid according to his work.

29.text: “Hear yet again — that one seed does not transform into another; let me tell you. If you sow wheat, will you reap barley? If you sow cumin, will you reap flax?

30.text: “And from the kind of plants: if you plant a fig, will it grow into almond for you? If you plant a walnut, will it sprout into a vine for you?

31.text: “If you plant sweet fruit, will it sprout as bitter? If you plant bitter fruit, will it sprout as sweet?

32.text: “In just this way: if a sinner has died, can he become righteous at the resurrection? If a righteous person has died, can he become a sinner at the resurrection? Each shall be repaid as his work, according to the fruit of his work and the work of his hand; he shall not be judged for some other sin.

33.text: “The tree of Lebanon is planted; it puts forth tall and great branches; it withers and is shed unless the dew of Hermon falls upon it; its leaf does not flourish.

34.text: “The cedar also: if the winter rain has not fallen upon it, it is uprooted.

35.text: “In just this way: the dead do not rise unless the dew of life from God falls upon them.”

1.text: “For the valleys of Galaboh and the mountains of Lebanon — if the rain of mercy from God does not fall upon them — do not put forth grass for the cattle and for the wild beasts.

2.text: “The mountains of Gilead and the valleys of Elam do not give greenness for the goats and sheep that graze, and for the wild creatures — for the wild ass and the wild ox, and for the gazelle.

3.text: “In the same way — apostates and heretics who have made their possession of denial and error from the beginning, if God’s dew of mercy has not come down upon them, the dead do not rise. The idol-worshipers, and root-chewers, those who contrive matters that they may quarrel — Cyprus and Damascus,

4.text: “the root-chewers, sorcerers and conjurers, and slayers of men,

5.text: “those who, having gone out from the law, lust greedily; who trust in their idol — the men of Athens and of Media, those who play lyres and timbrels and harps for their idols, who sing for them,

6.text: “who err with their idol, who pursue their lust by the work of their hand — these at the time of the resurrection, on the day of judgment, will not save themselves; these are they upon whom judgment shall fall.

7.text: “You foolish one, you of empty mind — does it seem to you that the dead do not rise?

8.text: “At the resurrection of the dead, when the trumpet is blown by the mouth of the archangel — by holy Michael — you shall not remain in your slumber. Therefore do not think this.

9.text: “Mountains and hills shall be made low; rivers and depths shall be made even; a way prepared shall come to be. [Isa 40:4]

10.text: “And for all flesh there shall be resurrection.”

1.text: “If it were not so — why is it that the fathers of old, beginning from Adam and from Abel and Seth, from Noah and Shem, from Abraham and Isaac, from Jacob and Joseph, from Moses and Aaron — did not desire to be buried outside the graves of their fathers?

2.text: “Was it not that at the resurrection they might rise together with their kin? That their bones should not be reckoned with the bones of the wicked who worship idols — with idol-worshipers and the heathen?

3.text: “But as for you — when many thousand upon thousand are buried in a single grave and their bones decay, saying, ‘How shall the dead rise after they are dead?’ — do not let your mind be deluded.

4.text: “When you look into a grave and no handful of earth is found, you say in your mind’s folly: ‘How shall the dead rise?’

5.text: “Will you say the seed you have sown does not sprout? Even the seed you have sown sprouts.

6.text: “In the same way, the souls God has sown — they shall rise speedily. Since he has brought man from non-existence into existence by his truth, he does not delay raising them with his life-giving word.

7.text: “Furthermore, he returns him from existence into death; furthermore, he returns him from death into existence.

8.text: “God is able to give life and to raise up.”

1.text: Hermon and her walls have fallen; for God has repaid them according to their wickedness and the work their hands have done. At that time, those who worship idols in Zebulun and Edom shall be brought low; for they have done so from their childhood and have not left it even to old age. Therefore Tyre and Sidon shall weep, since judgment is at hand against them for their idol and their wickedness.

2.text: And because they have wrought licentiousness and defilement and fornication, and worshiped idols, God shall avenge himself against them. And the daughters of Judah shall be brought low; for they have not stood firm in the commandment of God their Creator.

3.text: And likewise, at the resurrection, the shame of Jerusalem shall be revealed; for she did not walk in the law and judgment of God; but she lived in delight and in killing the righteous.

4.text: At that time, God will search her by the light of his wisdom; he will avenge himself for all she did in the days of her childhood, in the days of her youth — for all the wickedness she did not leave even to her old age.

5.text: Since they have lived in their custom and refused God’s commandment, since at the resurrection he shall avenge himself against them — like her former fathers, she shall enter the grave and become dust.

6.text: For Moses spoke concerning them: “Their vineyard is like the vineyard of Sodom.

7.text: “Their tendril is from Gomorrah; their cluster is a cluster of gall; their fruit is bitter.

8.text: “Their wine is the poison of serpents; even the poison of the deadly viper.” [Deut 32:32–33]

1.text: Daughter of Jerusalem! This is your shame which has been written by the prophet. Daughter of Jerusalem! Your work and your iniquity are like the work and iniquity of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah.

2.text: Your shame is as Gomorrah’s, as Sodom’s; the place of their vineyard was planted in lust and arrogance.

3.text: From fornication and arrogance, from violence and iniquity, from plunder and shedding of blood, from forgetting the name of God their Creator — except these, no rain of humility and mercy came down on them.

4.text: Except for their evil works and their idol, they have not known their Creator God; they are glad in the work of their hand; they fornicate with cattle and with man.

5.text: Their eyes have been blinded that they may not see; their ears have been deafened that they may not hear, that they may not do the will of God and what he loves. By their work they do not know God; they are the vineyard of Sodom; their offspring is also the tendril of Gomorrah, that bears no sweet fruit.

6.text: For from the day they were planted they have been planted with a curse, and their plantation was in the time of destruction; when they have pressed their vine, it becomes deadly poison.

7.text: For the planting of their vine has drunk Sheol’s water; their tendril has been hardened in the hot wind; their vine-tendril has no goodness for all time.

8.text: When it has borne fruit and is pressed, it has become for scourge and for destruction; it hardens the minds of those who drink it; it makes them perverse and far from God.

9.text: And by their evil work they live; he makes them a dwelling for the Devil. The Sodomic tendril begins to consume; she climbs up to the mountains and to the trees.

10.text: And the idol of those around her she covers with her shade; to demons who know neither evil nor good, she sacrifices her daughters and her sons.

11.text: And they pour out innocent blood; from Sodomic wine they have made an eternal pouring, and to the idol they pour out.

12.text: She honors and worships Dagon whom the Ammonites worship.

13.text: That she may sacrifice to them and do their will: from her childhood till her youth, then from her old age till the day of her death — always, from the cattle of her flock the fattened ones she sacrifices to them; rejoicing in the demons’ drink and folly which they have taught her, that she may not know God her Creator who has fed her and cared for her always.

14.text: Furthermore — “At the time of the resurrection I shall avenge myself against her; for she did not turn back to my law, did not endure faithfully in my commandment; her time shall be unto eternity.

15.text: “If her gods are truly her creators, then when I was angry with her in my wrath, when I separated from her those friends who fornicate with her, let them rise up and run to Gehenna and save her.

16.text: “As she rendered insult and shame against my house and against the vessels of my sanctuary, so among all I have made her a wretched outcast.

17.text: “Behold, this is the people of God; it is the house of God, Creator of Israel; it is the dwelling-place of the name of the Most High. Yet though it is called ‘set apart of the set apart’ and ‘city of the king of glory — Jerusalem’ — she has grieved my name by which she was named.

18.text: “As she was my servant and I her Lord, she boasts in me; but she points the finger at me like a criminal, and is not one who fears me as her Lord and does my will.

19.text: “She has become a stumbling-block to lead astray; she submits to other gods who do not feed her or rear her or clothe her, instead of those who do.

20.text: “She sacrifices to them; she eats their sacrifice; she pours out the drink-offering for them; she drinks the drink-offering; she burns incense for them; she breathes the fragrance of the incense for them; they command her; she submits to them.

21.text: “Again she sacrifices her sons and her daughters to them; she shouts for joy at her love for them, and is glad in the work of her hand and in the speech of her lips.

22.text: “On the day of judgment, woe to her! Woe to the gods she loves and embraces! Together with them she shall descend to that uttermost Sheol where the worm does not sleep and the fire is not quenched.”

23.text: “Wretched daughter of Jerusalem, woe to you — for you have forsaken me who created you and have worshiped other gods.

24.text: “And I shall bring upon you the recompense of your work; you have grieved me, you have despised my word, you have not made your work right; according to your provocation I shall avenge myself.

25.text: “For you have grieved my word; in my commandment which I commanded you that you might keep, that I might dwell with you, that I might save you from all who attack you — in my covenant in which I swore with you — you have not stood firm. Therefore I disregard you; I shall not save you speedily.

26.text: “All this you have not kept; and I have disregarded you. In the time of judgment also I shall avenge myself against you. Am I not the one who created you? You have not kept my word and my commandment; I had honored you, that you might be of my people.

27.text: “Sodom and Gomorrah were separated; you also have separated yourself from me.

28.text: “I destroyed them in my wrath; you are of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah whom I destroyed; by going to a young man’s wife, by lying with women, by lusting against the law with cattle and with man, those whom I created have grieved me; therefore the calling of their name have I destroyed from the earth, that they should not live in their pleasure.

29.text: “From the least to the greatest, there is no fearing of God before them; they assist him [Satan] in every evil work; not one of them rebukes another to leave off doing that work; for their work is evil; they are sated with iniquity and transgression.

30.text: “All evil work — plunder and arrogance, greed — is prepared in their thought.

31.text: “Therefore God disregarded them; he overturned their cities; some he burned with fire to their foundations; they perished utterly forever, and not one of them remained.

32.text: “For they are bound in sin; until the great day of judgment when the eternal judgment shall be given, they shall await; in their evil work they have grieved me, and I shall not have mercy on them and shall not forgive them.

33.text: “I also disregarded them. In the same way, you, wretched daughter of Jerusalem — at the time of judgment, like them, you shall be bound. For all your work is plunder and sin, lust and greed, and speaking lies; and since it is the path of error and slipping which I do not love, when I take hold of you in my anger you shall find no excuse.

34.text: “I had made you for honor; but you made yourself for shame. I had made you for myself; but you became for another.

35.text: “I had betrothed you for holiness; but you became for the Devil; and I shall avenge myself against you as is the wickedness of your work.

36.text: “Because you have not heard all my word, because when I loved you, you did not keep the commandment I commanded you — for I am God who created you — I shall multiply heavy vengeance against you; and against all sinners like you I shall be angry; according to their wickedness I shall repay them on the day of judgment.

37.text: “You have not kept my word; and you have disregarded my judgment; together with them I shall punish you.

38.text: “You who have no fearing of God in your hearts — Sodom and Gomorrah — woe to you!

39.text: “In the fire of Gehenna, woe also to your sister who shall be judged with you in unity — the daughter of Jerusalem; for to Gehenna prepared with no exit forever, you shall descend together; and woe to all who do your work.

40.text: “For you have not kept my word and my commandment; and you who have not kept my word and my commandment — you and she — at the time of judgment shall descend together to Sheol.

41.text: “But the righteous who have kept my word and my commandment shall eat what the sinners fattened; what the wicked plundered, the good shall divide as God has commanded; and the righteous and the good shall rejoice; they shall be glad.

42.text: “But sinners and transgressors shall weep; for all the wickedness they did, going out from my commandment, they shall be in grief.

43.text: “Whoever keeps my word and walks in my commandment — he is the one who shall receive my blessing, and shall be honored before me.

44.text: “Whoever keeps my word and does my commandment shall eat the blessing of the earth; he shall enter to where the good and upright kings have gone, and there he shall dwell.”

1.text: “In the time when I take hold of them in my wrath they shall be humbled; they shall be scourged. To Tyre and Sidon who today exalt themselves, and to all the districts of the land of Judah — woe to them!

2.text: “For God said: ‘A son of destruction, arrogant and proud, the enemy of righteousness — one who stiffens his neck, who boasts and does not know his Creator — shall come forth from among them; and I, God who rules all, have made him the likeness of my wrath, that I may show forth my power against him.’

3.text: “This Capernaum, Samaria and Galilee, Syria and Damascus, Cyprus and Achaia, and all the heathen of the district of the Jordan — these are a people who have stiffened their necks, who walk in their custom, whom the shadow of death and darkness has covered; for the Devil has covered their mind, and they submit to that arrogant one; they do not turn back to the fear of God.

4.text: “To those who submit to the impure, and to those who sacrifice in their name — woe to them at that time! For they have denied God their Creator; they are like beasts without understanding. For that godless son of destruction in every place will set up his image. In the work of his hand and the desire of his heart, in plunder and every sin, in deceit and transgression, in plunder and every fornication a man works, in lying speech — he is glad.

5.text: “Since it has been counted before God that he should do this, it is made known in his time that he shall do so.

6.text: “The sun shall darken; the moon shall become blood; the stars shall fall from heaven; according to the work of the hands of those who dwell in it, that earth and all that is in it may pass away by the sign which shall come in the latter days. All his work shall perish;

7.text: “For God has glory over the creation he created; in one hour, as he wills, he has done it; and the last enemy, death, he shall abolish.

8.text: “For God who rules all has said, ‘I will avenge’; and after that there is no rule [for the enemy].

9.text: “And in the day when he is taken hold of in my wrath, he shall descend to the scourging and judgment that have been kept ready for him; he shall draw with him into destruction, affliction, and denial all those who are with him. For I am the one who brings forth from and brings into the judgment of Gehenna.

10.text: “Let not the mighty boast in his strength; for he gives firmness and strength to weary men; and again, to mighty and strong men he gives weariness.

11.text: “He is God who rules; and against those who do violence — judging from the hand of those who oppress them, he saves; he repays the vengeance of widows and orphans.

12.text: “To you, woman, who boast and stiffen your neck, woe to you. It seems to you that I shall not take hold of you in my wrath and avenge myself against you. As it was said in this manner: ’How is the dawn-star, which rises in the morning, fallen from heaven?

13.text: “In his arrogance and his pride: I will spread my throne in the heavens and above the stars; I will be like the Most High.’ [Isa 14:12–14]

14.text: “So you also have dared in your arrogance to speak; and you have not remembered God who created you and made you with his hand. By the firmness of your mind to descend to Gehenna — why have you exalted yourself?

15.text: “You have been humbled with all angels who are like you in your arrogance; for they in lowliness of heart praise their Creator, and do not go out from his commandment; for they have known that he is the one who created them and made them; they have kept their mind that they should not go out from his commandment or transgress.

16.text: “But you in the arrogance of your mind have done evil; you have become separated from your companions and humbled. For sinners and those of your nature who, like you, deny — those godless ones in whose dwelling is sin and iniquity, deceit and plunder — you are their keeper; you teach them wickedness; they go in your desire and your commandment.

17.text: “You and those whom you have led astray by your cunning shall descend together to Gehenna — woe to you.

18.text: “You children of God led astray by that misleading criminal — woe to you! For he and his demons taught you, and like him you have erred. To the scourging from which there is no exit forever, you shall descend together.

19.text: “At the beginning, while my servant Moses was yet alive — at Horeb and at the water of Meribah, at Mount Sinai and at Amalek — you grieved him.

20.text: “Again, when you sent spies to Canaan, and they told you: ‘The way is far; their walls reach to heaven; their fortress is strong; warriors dwell there’ — in your anger, you rebelled against God’s word, that you might return to the land of Egypt where you did the work of hardship.

21.text: “You did not remember God who saved you from affliction, who in Egypt did great wonders and led you by the hand of his angel. By day a cloud shielded you that the sun might not burn you; and a pillar of fire shone by night so that your foot might not stumble in darkness.

22.text: “When his army and Pharaoh terrified you, you cried out utterly to Moses; and Moses cried out utterly to God; and he kept you by his angel that you should not meet Pharaoh’s army.

23.text: “But them he turned back into affliction. ‘God alone led them, and there was no other god with them’ [Deut 32:12]. Their enemies he buried at one time in the sea; he left no fugitive of them.

24.text: “And Israel he brought across through the midst of the sea on foot; from the Egyptians no evil reached them. He brought them to Mount Sinai; and there for forty years he fed them with manna.

25.text: “For the sons of Israel always grieve God; though he had done so much good for them, they neglected to worship God.

26.text: “From their childhood till they grew old they kept wickedness in their mind. For the mouth of God in the book of the generations of the fathers spoke thus: ’The mind of the sons of Adam is ash; all their work is running to plunder and to wickedness; among them there is none who loves a straight work — except gathering with violence the wealth of others, swearing falsely, killing one’s neighbor, plundering and stealing.

27.text: “All in their lifetime go to this wickedness.’” And the sons of Israel who have broken God’s commandment, from the beginning to the end utterly grieved God.

1.text: And God baptized the earth with the water of the flood when he had punished the former peoples for the sin of the sons of Cain; he cleansed it of all the sin of the sons of Cain.

2.text: “I am grieved that I have created man,” he said, and destroyed all the transgressors. Except for eight people he left none; all he destroyed. After this he multiplied them; he filled the earth; and they divided the inheritance of their father Adam.

3.text: But Noah made a covenant with God — that God would not destroy the earth again with the water of destruction; and the children of Noah, that they should not eat that which has died or rotted, should not worship any other gods besides God who created them, that he should be their God, that he should not destroy them once again in vain, that he should not withhold from them the rains of summer-rain and the latter-rain, that he should give in their seasons food for cattle and for men, that he should give them grass and grain-fruit and plant — that they should make their work pleasing to God in all he loves — they made a covenant.

4.text: After he had given them this ordinance, the sons of Israel grieved God by their wickedness; they did not walk as their fathers — as Abraham and Isaac and Jacob — who did not break the law of God their Creator.

5.text: From the least to the greatest, those sons of Israel who did not keep the law of God were perverted in their work.

6.text: Their priests and their chiefs and their scribes — all of them — break God’s law.

7.text: They did not stand firm in the law and ordinance of God which Moses, in the book of the law, commanded them, saying: “Love God your Creator with all your heart and all your soul.

8.text: “Love your neighbor as yourself. Do not worship other gods. Do not go to a young man’s wife. Do not kill. Do not steal.

9.text: “Do not bear false witness. Do not desire your neighbor’s possessions — anything your brother has bought, his donkey or his ox.”

10.text: But after he had commanded them all this, those wicked sons of Israel turn again to sin and denial, to transgression and plunder, to the young man’s wife and to stealing, to lying and to worshiping idols.

11.text: The sons of Israel grieved God at Horeb by making the idol of a calf that goes out to grass; “Behold, these are our gods who brought us out of Egypt,” they said, and bowed down.

12.text: They rejoiced in the work of their hand; they ate, drank, were filled, and rose up to dance.

13.text: Therefore God said to him: “Your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, have sinned and gone astray; they have made the image of a calf and bowed down to the idol.” And Moses came down from Mount Sinai in anger.

14.text: Moses came down, raging against his people, with his attendant Joshua; and when Joshua heard, he said: “Behold, I hear the sound of warriors in the camp of Israel.”

15.text: And Moses said to Joshua: “It is not the sound of warriors but the sound of unfermented wine.” Coming down, he broke their image; he ground it utterly to dust; and the sons of Israel he made drink in the water near the mountain. [cf. Ex 32:17–20]

16.text: After this, because they had done evil before God, he commanded the Levites to slay one another.

17.text: Knowing that to contend with God exceeds killing oneself and one’s kin and fathers, they did as he commanded.

18.text: Therefore Moses said to them: “Because you have grieved God who fed you and cared for you and brought you out of the house of subjection — God who gave you the inheritance he swore to your fathers, to give to them and to their children after them — in your own hand you have made God pleased.”

19.text: Yet from that point onward they go to sin and evil; they did not leave off grieving God.

20.text: From their childhood through their youth to their old age — they are not like their fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who pleased God by their good works; that God should give them what is upon the earth and what in heaven he has prepared for those who love him — the milk-and-honey-flowing land of inheritance, and in the world to come the Paradise of joy prepared for the righteous — what eye has not seen, what ear has not heard, what has not entered the mind of man — which God has prepared for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and for those who love him and please him in their lifetime as their fathers did.

21.text: But the children of those, deniers and wicked, living in the desire of their mind, have not heard the word of God who fed them and cared for them and kept them from their childhood.

22.text: They did not remember God who brought them out of the land of Egypt and saved them from brick-making and bitter subjection.

23.text: But they grieved him utterly; therefore he raised against them the heathen who were around them; and they, rising in enmity, made them tributary as they pleased.

1.text: At that time, the men of Midian rose in enmity against them; they raised their armies to attack Israel. The name of their king was Akrandyos; he gathered the great armies of Syria and Cilicia and Damascus in the morning.

2.text: He encamped beyond the Jordan and sent messengers to Israel, saying: “Pay me tribute. Otherwise, I have come to punish you, to plunder your cattle, to take all your possessions, to lead your children away captive.

3.text: “I will lead you captive to a land you do not know; there I will make you water-carriers and wood-gatherers.

4.text: “As for your saying, ‘We are God’s people; none can overcome us’ — do not be confident. Is it not the case that God has sent me to destroy you, that I should plunder your wealth? He sent me, that I might gather all that is yours.

5.text: “Other peoples whom I have punished — have their strange idols saved them? I plundered their wealth and provision; them I killed; their children I led captive.

6.text: “In just the same way, if you do not bring me tribute as I have commanded, I will do to you as I did to them.” And he crossed the Jordan to plunder their cattle and their wealth, and to lead away their wives and children captive.

7.text: After this, the sons of Israel wept a bitter weeping to God; they cried out utterly; but they had none to help them.

8.text: Therefore God gave firmness to three brothers; their names are these: Mebkyus, Maqabis, and Yehuda. Of fair appearance, they were warriors in all their strength.

9.text: When the sons of Israel were heard weeping utterly, the cry of all the sons of Israel grieved their hearts; widows and orphans, their priests and their princes, all the people of Israel, women and boys — all were strewing ashes on their heads and weeping; their nobles were clothed in sackcloth.

10.text: But those fair-of-form and comely brothers agreed to go and save them. “Let us go,” they took counsel together, “and give our bodies to death for the sake of these people.”

11.text: Saying to each other, “Be of good courage! Be of good courage!” — girding their swords on their loins, taking their spears in their hands — they went; prepared to do battle with the warrior-king, they went.

12.text: They came upon him while he was seated at table; and Mebkyus struck the warrior — that he might not swallow what he had not chewed, with one stroke he cut off his neck. And Yehuda and Maqabis struck with the sword those who were at the king’s right and left.

13.text: And when their king had fallen, all fled; their spears entered into the breasts of their companions; their bows shattered; they were defeated.

14.text: But those fair-of-form, comely brothers were saved; nothing evil came upon them. For God had turned his scourging back upon them [the enemies]; and those wicked ones slew one another.

15.text: They were defeated and died. Until they had crossed the Jordan they cast aside all their wealth; everything that was theirs was left behind. And when the sons of Israel saw them fleeing and going to their camp, they took the plundered wealth for themselves.

16.text: So God by the hand of Mebkyus and his brothers thus saved the sons of Israel.

17.text: And the sons of Israel lived a few months pleasing God.

18.text: But after that, they returned again to their wickedness; the sons of Israel neglected to worship God as was fitting.

19.text: And he again grieved them by peoples they did not know — who gathered the harvest of their field, who destroyed the planting of their vine, who plundered their flock and slaughtered their cattle before them without sharing them,

20.text: who led away captive their wives, their sons, and their daughters. Because they always grieve God — for they are the people who have broken his law — they crush their children’s heads before their faces; and they cannot save them.

1.text: The people of Tyre and Sidon, dwelling on the seashore and across the Jordan river — in Gilead and Karan, in Canaan and Jebus, in the Girgashite and Edom — and the people of Amalek;

2.text: all the heathen in their countries and their tribes, in their ordinances and their districts, in the languages of their lands — all dwell as God has set them.

3.text: Of them, there are those whose work is good and who know God.

4.text: Of them, there are those whose work is evil, who do not know God who created them; and according to their work, he gave them into the hand of the king of Syria, Amenezer;

5.text: for he shall take the wealth of Damascus, and shall divide the plunder of Samaria before the king of Egypt.

6.text: The mountains of Gilead and the valleys of Galaboh, Samaria, and all of Pontus in the land of Judah; those who dwell in Arabia, in Media and Parthia, in Seleucia, and in the mountains of Cappadocia —

7.text: those who dwell in their districts, who do not know God and do not keep his commandment — these are a stiff-necked people.

8.text: And he will repay them according to the wickedness of their work and the work of their hand.

9.text: The district of Caesarea, the people of Gilead and of Amalek — they have agreed together to destroy the city of God which is full of righteousness, in which dwells the Holy One of Israel, who sits upon the chariot of cherubim, before whom stand the exceedingly many angels — the city in which the Lord of hosts is praised.

1.text: The armies of Edom and Amalek do not worship God, whose hand holds the rule of heaven and earth. They are criminals who do not walk in truth; therefore they do not fear to tread the temple [of God].

2.text: Apart from fornication and shedding of blood, eating animals struck by a paw or which have died of themselves and all such things — they have no fear of God before them. These are despised and defiled.

3.text: They have no faith and no good conduct; they hate good works; they do not know God. Apart from wickedness and plunder, defiled work and uproar of every kind — apart from songs and games as their father Sebelyanos taught them — they do not know the way of peace.

4.text: For he rules them with his demons; he teaches each of them every evil work — wickedness and plunder, snatching another’s wealth by force, theft, eating carrion and that which has been struck, and fornication.

5.text: And everything that resembles it — going to a young man’s wife, shedding blood, eating what is sacrificed to idols and what has died, killing the souls of men by violence, mocking and envy, greed, and every evil work that God does not love — he teaches them this teaching. To draw them far from the way of God who holds the whole world — their enemy Sebelyanos brings it upon them.

6.text: But the way of God is humility and meekness, loving the neighbor and not provoking the brother, mutual affection with every person, and peace.

7.text: Do not be those who show partiality to a man’s face; plunderers and rebels, snatchers, those who go to a young man’s wife, those who do violence and evil to their neighbor, those who deceive in order to wrong their neighbor in iniquity.

8.text: They point fingers; they shake themselves; they devise wickedness; they cast lots to lead men astray, that they may descend to eternal judgment.

1.text: Remember that you are going to God; all is in his hand; you shall stand before him so that he may judge you according to the work you have done.

2.text: In times past too there were the wicked and arrogant, those than whom none was greater or stronger — the sons of Re’ayt; thus they were. Because they saw their own strength and stature and the might of their arm, they did not set God before them; they did not know that he is their Creator who brought them out of non-existence.

3.text: And their fathers, while they were angels, used to praise God in heaven with the angels. But when their will led them astray, they descended to the eternal punishment of judgment.

4.text: They took wives from among the daughters of men; for God had created human flesh for them that he might test them — to test whether they would keep the law and commandment despite the arrogance of their mind.

5.text: But they did not keep the commandment; and he brought them down with their father the Devil to the Gehenna of fire; for God was angry with the angels who transgressed as men do; because of them the days of man have grown shorter.

6.text: And the sons of Adam they took with them; with their punishment they brought them down to Sheol.

7.text: Because the angels erred through the sons of Cain, the days of man have been shortened; whereas in the beginning the days of man were nine hundred, they were reduced to one hundred and twenty years.

8.text: And God said: “They are flesh and blood; my Spirit shall not abide upon them.” [Gen 6:3]

9.text: Therefore our days have been shortened; furthermore, because of our transgression and our sin, our days are fewer than those of our former fathers, and there are some who die in childhood.

10.text: But the days of our fathers were many, because they kept his commandment and did not grieve God.

11.text: They rebuked their daughters that they might teach them; they rebuked their sons that they might not transgress God’s commandment.

12.text: Therefore, together with their sons and daughters, because they did not break God’s commandment, their days were truly many.

1.text: When the sons of Cain multiplied, they made lyre and tambourine, harp and cymbal, games and song of every kind.

2.text: Furthermore — because she was beautiful, on account of whom the righteous Abel was killed — from his wife (whom Cain married after killing her husband) beautiful and comely daughters were born to Cain; for after killing his brother, he took her [as wife]; and she was his.

3.text: Taking them with him, he separated from his father and went westward to the valleys of Qefaz; and the children of that beautiful woman were beautiful like their mother.

4.text: Therefore the angels descended to the sons of Cain; they did not delay even an hour; they took for themselves as wives whomever they chose.

5.text: Therefore — because of their error, since they led us into error together with them — God was angry with us also and with them.

6.text: And the Devil, deceiving with the words “You shall become as gods, like God your Creator,” led our father Adam and our mother Eve into his error.

7.text: They in their ignorance — it seemed true to them — broke the commandment of their Creator who brought them from non-existence into existence, that they might bow down and praise his holy name.

8.text: Those who took the wealth of God for themselves — their Lord humbled them; and that arrogant one also he humbled.

9.text: As David said, “In a sinner’s arrogance the poor is set on fire” [cf. Ps 10:2 LXX] — for our father Adam by the Devil’s arrogance was judged in truth before his Creator God.

10.text: Likewise, by the sons of Cain the angels who erred took us into their error. Therefore the days God has given us are fewer than the days of our fathers.

11.text: But they had done good works; no evil approached them; for they had set their hearts firm on God; and they taught their sons and daughters not to deviate from the commandment of God which had been taught to them.

12.text: But they — even if they had done good works — if they had not told their children and taught them, it would not have benefited them.

13.text: As David said: “They did not hide from their children for another generation; they taught God’s glory, his power and wonders that he had done; that, as they remembered, they should teach their children; that they should pay attention and do; that they should commit God’s judgment as a trust to them; that by their moral conduct they should please God; that as their fathers had, they should keep his commandment. [Ps 78:4–7]

14.text: “In their childhood, fearing God and his judgment as they learned from their fathers, the commandment which their fathers committed to them as a trust they did not abandon.

15.text: “And their children — that they might make their conduct beautiful, and give honor to their Creator — learned from their fathers; for they kept his law and loved him.

16.text: “And he hears their prayer; he does not disregard their petition; for he is the forgiver.

17.text: “He multiplies the turning back of his wrath; in all his scourging he did not destroy.” [Ps 78:38]

1.text: Our brothers, take thought! Do not forget what they told you of old: that God preserves the righteousness of those who do good works.
