2.text: Upon the earth he multiplies their fruit; the calling of their name endures for good unto eternity; and their seed shall not lack grain upon the earth.

3.text: For he contends for them; he does not give them into the hand of their enemy; from the hand of their adversaries and from all their enemies who hate them, he saves them.

4.text: And to those who love his name, he is a helper in their time of affliction; he keeps them; he forgives all their sins.

1.text: David trusted in God; because he had believed in him, [God] became his refuge; and from the hand of King Saul he saved him.

2.text: When his son Absalom rose up; when the Philistines rose up; when the Amalekites and Edomites and Karniyonites rose up — because he had trusted in him and kept his law, God saved David from all the enemies who opposed him.

3.text: But the wicked kings who did not trust in him — God did not save; for victory is from God; in the hand of their enemies they were defeated.

4.text: Hezekiah trusted in God; and from the hand of the arrogant Assyrian he saved him.

5.text: But his son Manasseh did not put his trust in God; in the hand of his enemy he was defeated. Those enemies of his who defeated Manasseh were not like him; because he had not put his trust in God, and because he did not fear God who had honored and made him great — they bound him and led him to their country instead.

6.text: Because he had not made his way pleasing to his Creator God — that his days might be multiplied, that his enemy might contend on his behalf, that God might be strength and firmness for him before and after — [God] withheld from him the wealth he had given.

7.text: For it is better to trust in God than to trust in many armies and horses, in bow and shield.

8.text: And the man who trusts in him shall live; he shall be honored; he shall be utterly exalted.

9.text: God shows no partiality of face. Those who do not trust in God and trust in the abundance of their wealth — they shall be cast out from the grace and honor he gave them.

10.text: But those who trust in him he keeps. Those whom others call ignorant, he makes ignorant — because they have not steeled their hearts to follow God and keep his law; in their time of affliction, and when their enemies oppose them, he does not help them speedily.

11.text: But for the one who steels his heart in following God, in keeping his commandment and his law — for him he becomes a refuge in time of affliction.

12.text: By killing his enemy and capturing his enemy’s cattle, by capturing his enemy’s countrymen, by raining seasonable rains, by the fruit of the bud, by the gathering of the heap, by the fruit of his planted place,

13.text: by the fruit of summer-rain and winter-rain, by giving grass and freshness, by giving various fruits that those under his hand may be made glad — [God] makes him glad.

14.text: That they may eat the labor of others, that they may be filled with the plunder of their enemies, that they may plunder beasts, sheep, and cows, that they may eat and clothe themselves from another’s table, that they may take captive their enemies’ children — [God] makes them glad.

15.text: And God does all this for the one he loves; but the one he hates, he makes prey for his enemy.

16.text: He binds his hands and his feet; he casts him into his enemy’s hand; he makes him a mockery for his enemies. For the one who has broken God’s law has become a shedder of blood; therefore [God] is not pleased with the seed of his house.

17.text: And at the time of judgment he does not stand firm. When [God] repays evil to evildoers, he repays the doers of wickedness with the fruit of their work.

18.text: But to those who do good, he repays good; and it has been ordained from God that he should keep them by [the work of his own] hand.

19.text: And [man] was ordained to keep his commandment, to do his will, to praise God his Creator. For he is the servant over all his creation; for of all fleshly creatures, only man transgresses his Creator’s commandment.

20.text: All [other creatures] know him; and all who live according to their order are kept by his commandment and his law as he has commanded them.

21.text: But man dares against God who has set him over the beasts and the cattle and the birds and all his creation.

22.text: God gave to our father Adam all the creation he had created — whether what is in the sea or what is on the dry land. To do what he willed, that he might eat them on earth like grain, that he might rule them and put them to work, that beasts and cattle alike might obey man — God gave them; and that the kings of men might obey God who gave them honor, that they might bow and obey him — over all his creation he appointed them.

23.text: But if they go out from his law, he separates them from the wealth he gave them; for he rules heaven and earth, and to the one who does his will, he gives it.

24.text: Whom he wills, he appoints; and whom he wills, he removes. He kills and saves; he scourges and forgives.

25.text: There is no other like him; for he is Lord of all the creation he created, and there is none who finds fault with him. In heaven above, on earth beneath, there is no other God besides him.

26.text: He appoints and removes; he kills and saves; he scourges and forgives; he impoverishes and enriches.

27.text: He receives the petition of those who petition him; the prayer of those who do his will with a pure heart, he hears; he does their will in all that they have asked.

28.text: Great and small he makes obey them; in the mountains and hills, in the caves and forests, in the pit of the earth, in sea and land — all that is in them is theirs.

29.text: To those who do the will of their God, all is theirs; from his blessing he does not deprive them; the wages of their praise he gives them.

30.text: And in heaven, to their fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, to David and Hezekiah, to Samuel — those who did not go out from his law and his commandment — he gives the honor he has prepared;

31.text: that he may give them the inheritance he swore to their fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob from of old, who served him; and that they may be made glad in his kingdom.

1.text: Take thought of the names of those who do good works; do not forget their work.

2.text: Strive that your name may be as their names — that in the light-dwelling he has prepared for the good kings and princes who did the will of God, you may be glad with them.

3.text: Furthermore — know and understand the names of the evil kings and princes who shall be judged, and who shall be reckoned to shame even among men after their death.

4.text: For though seeing and hearing, they did not make their way pleasing to God; they shall be judged together with the godless and the deniers who did God’s will [outwardly only].

5.text: As for you — be gracious and meek and upright; do not walk in the path of the godless with whom God is angry.

6.text: Judge truly; vindicate the widow and the orphan; save them from the hand of the sinners who plunder them.

7.text: Stand for the orphan as a father, that you may save him from the hand of the plunderer. Be terrified when the orphan’s tears fall before your face — that you may not be terrified by the sea of fire in which unrepentant sinners shall sit.

8.text: Direct your foot toward the way of peace; seek peace and follow her. For the eyes of God are toward the righteous, and his ears toward their petition.

9.text: But God’s face is against those who do evil — that he may destroy their memorial from the earth; and no man hiding on mountain or rampart he leaves behind.

10.text: “Until I have destroyed those who do not keep my word, I will not turn back my face. For I, the LORD, am a jealous one who avenges those who hate me and do not keep my word.

11.text: “And those who honor me and keep my word, I will honor.”

1.text: Do not walk in the way of Cain — who killed his brother, who in meekness had followed him, trusting that he loved him.

2.text: He killed his brother out of jealousy over a woman. Those who work iniquity and jealousy and denial against their neighbor are like him.

3.text: They went in the way of Cain — not in the way of meek Abel; for Abel was meek as a sheep, and his blood, in the purity of his heart, was as the blood of an innocent lamb sacrificed to God. But those who go in the way of meek Abel love God.

4.text: As Abel was meek, so God loves everyone who walks in meekness — as the righteous and meek Abel.

5.text: But the wicked God disregards; their judgment awaits them on their neck; on their shoulder it is written. At the time of judgment, before the angels and men and all his creation, it shall be read out.

6.text: Then the deniers and rebels who have not done God’s will shall be ashamed.

7.text: And a dreadful word shall be given to them: “Cast them into the fire of Gehenna which has no exit forever.”

1.text: When Gideon trusted in God, with a small army he defeated the uncircumcised heathen army — a great host, like locusts beyond counting.

2.text: “Kings and princes! There is no other God besides me; do not trust in other gods.

3.text: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of your mother’s womb, who raised you, who fed you, who clothed you. Why do you grieve me? Why do you worship another god besides me?

4.text: “All this I did for you; and what did you give me? What do I seek from you? Nothing but the salvation of your souls — that you may walk in my law and ordinance, in my commandment; and that I might give you the salvation of your souls.

5.text: “God who rules all has said: ‘Save yourselves from idol and from divination and from sorcery.’

6.text: “Upon those who do this and those who hear them, upon those who do their will and become their friends, upon those who walk in their commandments — God’s scourge shall come.

7.text: “For peoples whom you do not know and who do not pity you shall rise against you. If you do not do the will of God your Creator — as the prophets said, from the prophet Samuel onward; as Ezekiel and Enoch and Asaph spoke — they shall eat the fruit of your labor.

8.text: “And he said: ’Evil men will come, changing their clothes. Apart from eating and drinking, apart from adorning themselves with silver and gold, apart from doing every work God does not love — they have no other law.

9.text: “They are prepared to go to food and drink; from the time they rise from their sleep, from morning till evening they run to evil work. In their path is wretchedness and destruction; their feet have no way of peace.

10.text: “They do not know the way of peace; before their eyes there is no fear of God; without faith and conduct, they are perverse and wicked — greedy, gluttonous and drunken, intoxicated, and their iniquity is lawless. To licentiousness and shedding of blood, to theft and denial, to plundering another’s wealth by violence — they go.

11.text: “They condemn without judgment and without law; for they do not fear God who created them; therefore there is no shame before them.

12.text: “They do not respect the faces of those they see; they do not respect grey-haired and elders. When they hear of the wealth of the world, before they have seen it with their eyes they make it their own; for before their eyes there is no fear of God, and when they see it with their eyes, it is as if they had eaten it with their mouth.

13.text: “And their princes consume entrusted wealth. For they are deniers, and there is no truth in their mouth — what they said in the morning, they do not repeat in the evening.

14.text: “They neglect the cry of the poor and the hungry; they do not save the foreigner from the hand of those who plunder them; their disturbing kings hasten to wickedness.

15.text: “Therefore — let kings save the oppressed and the foreigner; let them not be those who deny justice.’”

16.text: But they are criminals who exact tribute and drink blood; their way is evil; they have no pity when they eat the calf with its mother or the bird with its chicks; all they see and hear they make their own.

17.text: They love to gather for themselves; they do not pity the sick and the poor; in violence they snatch another’s wealth; that they may stuff themselves in their house and be glad in it, they gather all they find.

18.text: Like one who has come up from a pit and his trace cannot be found, like one who does not return to his house, like swift ash they shall perish. Because in their lifetime they did no good works, when God seizes them in his anger — woe to their soul.

19.text: When God disregards them, as they are by themselves they perish at once; for God endures them [in patience] in case they should turn in repentance — for he does not hasten to destroy; in their own time they perish.

20.text: But if they do not turn in repentance, like the ancients before them who did not properly keep God’s commandment, he destroys them.

21.text: They eat human flesh and drink human blood. Going to sin they gird themselves with violence; before them there is always no fear of God; from the moment they rise from their bed they do not rest from working iniquity.

22.text: Upon the earth, that they may destroy the lives of many — their work is eating and drinking, running to wickedness and destruction.

1.text: “Their way is perverse; for all go on the misleading way of Satan; therefore the LORD of all says: ‘In the time when I take hold of her in my wrath, woe to her body.’

2.text: “They do not know God’s way; they have turned it behind them; they have despised my law.

3.text: “And I, in the latter time of fulfillment, will repay them according to the wickedness of their work. At the time of judgment, as the wickedness of their work is written before me, I will avenge myself; for I am the LORD who kills and saves, who scourges and forgives — they cannot escape from my hand.

4.text: “For I, the LORD, fill from horizon to horizon; all creation is in my hand. Below the earth and above the heaven, in the sea and in the deeps of the waters — there is none who escapes from my hand.

5.text: “Below the earth I command the serpent; in the sea, the fish; in the air, the birds; in the wilderness, the wild ass. From horizon to horizon all is mine.

6.text: “For it is I who work wonders and signs before me; in heaven above and on earth beneath, none escapes my hand. There is none who says to me, ‘Where will you go? What will you do?’

7.text: “I command the archangels and the host; every name that is called is mine; the birds of heaven, the wild beasts of the forest, all the cattle — all are mine.

8.text: “The south wind and the summer-heat rise up; the Red Sea, in the latter days, shall be parted because of the splendor coming upon it.

9.text: “For he rules the living and the dead, from Noba and Saba, from Ethiopia and Hindekē, with all their districts and borders.

10.text: “With the rod that is in his hand, in meekness he keeps all; his rod is greater than all rods; with his rod he keeps his sheep.

11.text: “His horn is greater than all horns; his kingdom is exalted above all kingdoms; his authority rules the whole world; he is all-powerful; nothing is impossible for him.

12.text: “Above, he commands the clouds; below, he sprouts grass for the cattle; upon his shoots he gives fruit.

13.text: “As he wills, he feeds all according to their kinds; with their own food he feeds all he created — below the earth for the ant and the kubkuba* (mole?), above the earth for the wild beasts and the cattle. To him who prays he gives [the answer to] his prayer; the petition of widows and orphans he does not disregard.*

14.text: “Rather, in every time, the prayer of the pure ones who pray to him he receives. For the iniquity of evil men is as gathered wind, and the assembly of the wicked as mist.

15.text: “Their joy is as a fleeing bird; the comeliness of their countenance, of silver and gold, perishes on earth — it is a sham for the godless. Their gold does not profit them; the moth eats their garments.

16.text: “The heap of grain and wheat is eaten by worm and weevil; all passes like the day that passed yesterday; as a word that has gone out from the mouth does not return, so is the wealth of sinners. Their fine living is a passing shadow; the wealth of sinners before God is like a borrowed garment.

17.text: “But the righteous, even if they prosper, God does not disregard. Having mercy on the poor, hearing the judgment of orphans and the needy, clothing the naked from their own garments, not withholding from foreigner and hungry from the household wealth God has given them — they have grown rich [for this purpose].

18.text: “They do not pervert the judgment of the illiterate; they do not delay the wage of the hired servant. For the word of God, like a two-edged sword, is true and honored — in the count of months and in the measure of weights, they do not do iniquity.”

1.text: “But the poor again take thought in their beds; if the rich do not receive them, they become like dry wood without freshness; without moisture the root does not flourish; and without root the leaf does not flourish.

2.text: “For the leaf serves to adorn the fruit; if the leaf does not flourish, it bears no fruit. The head of a man is the fruit of righteousness; that which has no fruit has no good work.

3.text: “If he does righteousness, he bears uprightness; and God is pleased with the man who works truth and uprightness.

4.text: “To him who prays, he gives [the answer to] his prayer and the reward of his mouth; and the righteous he does not wrong on account of the righteousness he has done.

5.text: “For God is righteous, and he loves righteousness; the sinner he does not justify without repentance for the evil work he has done. The soul of every man is held in his hand; and he rules heaven and earth; in judgment he shows no partiality to rich or to poor.”

1.text: He created the whole world from non-existence; he prepared the mountains and the hills utterly; he established the earth upon water. That it might not be shaken, he bounded it with sand. For at the beginning, God’s word said: “Let there be light.”

2.text: The world being in darkness, light came to be; and God did his work; in fitness and proportion he prepared and established the world; he said: “Let there be evening and darkness”; and evening and darkness came to be.

3.text: And again God said: “Let there be light.” It dawned; and light came to be. The upper water he lifted up to heaven.

4.text: Like a tent he stretched it out; with wind he established it; the lower water he set under the deep of the sea.

5.text: The lock of the sea he shut with sand; that they should not sink down he established them with his Spirit; in it he placed the wild beasts and the cattle, and the great creatures; he placed in it the countless ones, the seen and unseen.

6.text: On the third day God created upon the earth the plants, all the grass, the trees, and the fruits that bear each according to its kind —

7.text: beautiful to behold and sweet to eat. He created the tree of life, and grass, and every plant whose seed is within it. For cattle and wild beasts and birds he created food; for all that he had created, he gave food.

8.text: Evening came; morning came; on the fourth day God said: “Let there be light in the firmament of heaven.” And God created the sun, the moon, and the stars. That they might shine upon the earth, and feed day and night, he set them in the firmament of heaven.

9.text: After this the sun, moon, and stars, day and night, took their turns.

10.text: On the fifth day God created all the wild beasts and animals that dwell in the water, all the birds that fly in heaven, the seen and the unseen — all this God created.

11.text: On the sixth day he created beasts and cattle and worms; and having created and prepared all, he created Adam in his image and his likeness.

12.text: He gave him to reign over the beasts and the cattle he had created; furthermore, he gave him the cattle and beasts, the fish, and the leviathans of the sea.

13.text: All the cows on earth, the sheep, every animal seen and unseen, he gave him.

14.text: And Adam, whom he had created in his image and likeness, he set in Paradise. To eat, to tend the Garden, there to praise God — he commanded him.

15.text: That he should not break God’s commandment, he commanded him not to eat from the tree which brings death, which makes known evil and good.

16.text: For he said: “When you eat from that tree, you shall surely die.”

17.text: Our mother Eve, deceived by the serpent’s deception, ate from that tree of the fig; and she gave it to our father Adam.

18.text: And he ate from that tree; and upon himself and his children he brought death.

19.text: For he broke his commandment; because he had eaten from that tree from which God had commanded him not to eat — God was angry with our father Adam; he drove him out of Paradise and sent him forth. That he might till her — and with the sweat of his face eat the wages of his labor — when he broke his commandment, God gave him the very earth which was cursed on his account, which brings forth thistle and thorn.

20.text: And when God brought him out into this earth, Adam returned to sorrow and to the brooding of the heart. To till the earth, in the sweat of his face, in toil and labor, he began to eat.

1.text: After this his children multiplied. Of them, there were those who praised God and honored him, who did not break his commandment.

2.text: There were prophets who spoke what was and what was to be. Of his children there were also sinners who spoke falsehood and wronged men. Cain, Adam’s firstborn, became evil; he killed his brother Abel.

3.text: Because he had killed his brother Abel, God was greatly angry with Cain; and because she had drunk his blood, God was angry with the earth.

4.text: And God said to Cain: “Where is your brother Abel?” And Cain, in the pride of his heart, said: “Am I my brother Abel’s keeper?”

5.text: Abel was righteous; but Cain, by killing the good man Abel his brother, became a sinner.

6.text: Furthermore, a righteous Seth was born; for Adam had begotten thirty daughters and thirty sons. Of them there were the good; and there were the wicked.

7.text: Of them, there were prophets and righteous ones; of them, there were sinners and deceivers.

8.text: Of them, there were the good and blessed who fulfilled their father Adam’s will; from Adam onward — down to the righteous Noah who kept God’s commandment — they fulfilled all that he had told his son Seth.

9.text: And he [Noah] caused his sons to keep God’s law; and as their father Noah had told them, he charged them: that they too should tell their children, and that they should keep God’s law.

10.text: And they, after them, lived teaching their children.

11.text: But Satan, when he had brought their fathers to the grave, dwelt in the idols that bore their images, and lived inflicting [harm] and speaking to people who consented to him; and they did all that the wicked teacher commanded.

12.text: They lived worshiping idols according to their custom until righteous Abraham — who fulfilled God’s will — arose.

13.text: And God made a covenant with him with fire and whirlwind. For he had first separated himself from his kindred, walking in the way of righteousness.

14.text: And God swore to him and to his children to give them the land of inheritance forever.

15.text: Likewise, to Isaac he swore to give him the inheritance of his father Abraham; and to Jacob likewise, to give him the inheritance of his father Isaac.

16.text: After them, their seed — Jacob’s sons of the twelve tribes of Israel — he made into kings and priests; he blessed them. “Be many, even of many,” he said.

17.text: And the inheritance of their fathers he gave them. But while he was feeding them, while he was loving them in all things — they did not leave off grieving God.

18.text: When he destroyed them, at that time they sought him; turning back, they ran to God; and God, because he loved them, forgave them.

19.text: Not for their own sake, but for their fathers’ sake; for he is merciful and forgiving to all he created.

20.text: That he may satisfy the hungry body, he stretches forth his right hand with blessing; that he may multiply grain for food, he opens his eye in mercy.

21.text: To the raven’s chicks and to all that call upon him, he gives food. When they cry to him, he saves the sons of Israel from the hand of their enemies.

22.text: But they return to grieve him; therefore he sends the heathen around them; and they destroy them, kill them, take them captive.

23.text: Again they cry to God in shouting and weeping; and he sends a helper. There was a time he saved by the hand of the prophets.

24.text: There was a time he saved by the hand of the judges. And when they grieved God, their enemies subjugated them and led them captive.

25.text: David arose and saved them from the hand of the Philistines. Again they grieved God; and he raised against them those who troubled them.

26.text: There was a time he saved by the hand of Jephthah; and again they forgot God who had saved them. Because God had brought their recompense upon them, he sends wicked enemies who afflict them and utterly take them captive.

27.text: Again, when they were afflicted, they cried to him; and he saved by the hand of Gideon. Again, by the work of their hand, they grieved God.

28.text: Again he sent against them those who tormented them; turning back, they wept and cried to God.

29.text: Again he saved by the hand of Samson; and they rested a little. From the wickedness they had done before, they arose to grieve God.

30.text: Again he sent against them others who afflicted them. Again they cried to God that he might send them a helper; they wept; and he saved by the hand of Barak and Deborah.

31.text: Again, worshiping God, they lived a few years; again they forgot him; in their earlier wickedness they grieved God.

32.text: And he sent against them others who afflicted them; again he saved them by the hand of Judith; again, after they had remained a few months, they rose to grieve God in their wickedness as before.

33.text: And he raised against them the heathen who ruled them; and they cried to God; they wept; and by the hand of Matatyu and his sons he saved them at the corner of the house.

34.text: For Aḥimelek, who came to attack the land of Judah, struck the head of the giant [re’aytawi]; and when that giant died, his army was scattered; they fled. The sons of Israel struck them as far as the Jabbok; not one of them was left to flee.

35.text: After this, having remained a little, they rose to grieve God; and he raised against them the heathen who ruled them; and they cried to God; they wept. But because they had always grieved God, and had forgotten his law, God disregarded their cry and their weeping.

36.text: They took them captive with their priests to the land of the Chaldeans.

37.text: There, doing sin and worshiping idols, those deniers — the sons of Israel — did not leave off grieving God; and with the heathen who had taken them captive, they mingled.

38.text: And God in his anger, that he might destroy them at once on account of their sin in that place, put wrath in the mind of King Artaxerxes — that he might not leave their children behind, from India to Ethiopia, in the land of Persia. The king having put a thousand pieces of gold into his treasury, he announced that on a fixed day he would destroy them.

39.text: And he did so: by the king’s permission he wrote a letter of decree, and gave him the seal that was in his hand to convey it to the land of Persia.

40.text: As the king commanded, on the one day on which it pleased him to destroy them, he gave him the seal. Their plunder, the gold and silver, was commanded to be brought into the king’s treasury.

41.text: Then, when the sons of Israel heard this, they cried utterly to God; they wept. They told Mordecai; and Mordecai told Esther.

42.text: And Esther said: “Fast! Pray! All the people of the sons of Israel — wherever you are, cry to God.”

43.text: And Mordecai put on sackcloth; he scattered dust on his head; and the sons of Israel in their land fasted; they prayed; they repented.

44.text: Esther wept exceedingly. Though she was queen, she put on sackcloth; she scattered dust; she shaved her head; she did not anoint herself with perfume as the Persian queens are accustomed to do; with deep heart she cried to God the Creator of her fathers; she wept.

45.text: Therefore, in the presence of King Artaxerxes of Persia, [God] gave her favor; and for her fathers’ Creator she made a great banquet.

46.text: The king and Haman entered the banquet which Esther had prepared. There, what Haman had wished to do against Mordecai — God repaid the recompense to Haman; on a tall tree they hanged him.

47.text: That Israel should be left as they wished, that they should not be made tributary, should not be plundered, should not be wronged, and that their property should not be taken from them — the king’s letter was issued.

48.text: That their land should not be destroyed, that their cattle should not be taken captive, but that in all the land of Persia they should be loved and honored — the letter was issued. For when in repentance they cried out to him in petition, God forgives Israel in this way.

49.text: And when they grieve him, he raises the heathen who afflict them; at that time, that he may send them a helper, that he may save them from the hand of the heathen who oppress them — they weep utterly; they cry out.

1.text: And when the men of Egypt afflicted the sons of Israel with hardship — by making them build bricks, in all the work they made them do, by making them tread mud without straw —

2.text: when overseers urging on the workers were appointed and they oppressed them, they cried out to God to save them from making all the brick of Egypt.

3.text: Then he sent them Moses and Aaron to help them. For God had sent them to bring his people out of the dwelling of Pharaoh’s tyranny, the king of Egypt; they saved them from brick-work. For in his arrogance he had refused to send Israel away that they might serve God and offer sacrifice in the wilderness.

4.text: And because God disregards the arrogant, on account of his arrogance he drowned Pharaoh together with his army in the Red Sea.

5.text: So also with kings and princes — those who disregard God’s word, who do not do his will, who do not give their wages to those who serve in good things, who do not honor his exalted name: all whom he appoints and makes king, those who do not do good — he disregards.

6.text: “If they make my kingdom straight, I will make their kingdom straight, says God who is all-powerful.

7.text: “Do good to me, and I will do good to you; keep my commandment, and I will keep your body. Walk in my commandment, and I will walk according to your mind.

8.text: “Love me, and I will love your life. Draw near to me, and I will strengthen you.

9.text: “Trust in me, and I will save you, says God who is all-powerful.

10.text: “Do not walk crosswise. Draw near to me, and I will draw near to you; for I love straight ways, says God who is all-powerful. Sinners and deniers, cleanse your hands; remove the wickedness of your mind;

11.text: “and I will remove my wrath from you; in forgiveness and mercy I will return to you.

12.text: “And I will remove from you the enemies — the criminals who work iniquity — even as I saved my servant David from the great cunning of the enemies who met him: from the hand of the warrior Goliath, from the hand of Saul who sought to kill him, and from the hand of his son Absalom who wished to take his kingdom —

13.text: “so also those who keep my law and fulfill my will, I will save like him; I will give them honor as their inheritance; in this world and the world to come, I will appoint them over all that they may be made glad.”

14.text: While he was yet a child, from his childhood God had chosen him for his pleasing way of life — he shall be one with the blessed kings who, in their pleasing way of life, served God; as Samuel did.

15.text: While he was yet serving in the dwelling of the Lord God, [God] told the prophet Samuel — that he might tell the aged priest Eli, whose work was good.

16.text: And when he had grown up serving in God’s house, by God’s command [Samuel] appointed his people and anointed their kings. For God had loved that the people he had chosen from the sons of Israel be appointed; and so, when [Samuel] had fulfilled the will of God who had created him, God gave him in his hand the anointing of kingship.

17.text: And while Saul was in his kingship, God said to the prophet Samuel: “I have loved David the son of Jesse, born of the tribe of Judah; go and anoint him.”

1.text: “Because he transgressed my word and grieved me, I hated the house of Saul.

2.text: “And I disregarded him; and because again he did not keep my word, I will not make a king from his kindred.

3.text: “Likewise, from those who do not keep my word, who do not walk in my law and ordinance — I will withhold my kingdom and my gift from their children unto eternity.

4.text: “When I exalted them, they did not exalt me; when I honored them, they did not honor me; therefore I shall destroy them and not return to honor them again.

5.text: “When I did good for them, they did not for me; when I forgave them, they did not forgive on my behalf.

6.text: “When I made them rulers over all, they did not make me ruler; when I honored them above all, they did not honor me; they did not keep my commandment.

7.text: “And I have taken from them the gift I gave; in my anger as I have sworn, I will not return it to them. God who is all-powerful says thus: ’Him who honors me, I will honor; him who loves me, I will love. [1 Sam 2:30]

8.text: “Those who do not honor me and have not kept my law, I will separate from the gift I gave them.

9.text: “God who is all-powerful says thus: ’Him who loves me, I will love; him who magnifies me, I will magnify.

10.text: “For I, the LORD, am all-powerful; in heaven above and on earth beneath, there is none who escapes my hand. The one who kills and saves, who scourges and forgives — I am the LORD.

11.text: “Honor and majesty are mine; whom I love, I honor; whom I hate, I bring low; for it is I who judge and avenge.

12.text: “Those who love me and call upon my name always — I am the one who forgives. For the rich and the poor, I am the one who feeds.

13.text: “Not man alone; but birds and beasts, fish in the sea and wild creatures, even serpents — I feed.

14.text: “Crocodiles and leviathans, shikoko* and hippopotami, the swift one — I feed.*

15.text: “All that moves in water, all that flies in the air — is mine.

16.text: “In all that is fitting and necessary, I am the one who feeds all who seek me.”

1.text: “Kings do not reign without my will; the hungry-fasters do not become poor without my command; the mighty do not grow strong without my command.

2.text: “I gave David favored-status, and to Solomon I gave wisdom; to Hezekiah I added years.

3.text: “To Goliath I shortened his days; to Samson I gave strength; again, I made his strength weak.

4.text: “My servant David I saved from the hand of the giant Goliath.

5.text: “Furthermore, from the hand of King Saul, and likewise from the hand of another giant who opposed him, and from the hand of all who opposed and hated him — I saved him; for he kept my commandment.

6.text: “And I loved him. Kings and princes who keep my commandment I love; for they have pleased me, I give them strength and victory over their enemies.

7.text: “Furthermore, that they may inherit the land of their fathers, the bright and free inheritance which I swore to their fathers, I give them.”

1.text: “You also, kings and princes — hear my word; keep my commandment, says God who is all-powerful. Whom I have kept and saved, whom from their parents onward I have raised, whom in all they sought I have fed,

2.text: “whom I have brought into the harvest of the land, whom I have fed fittingly with the blessing of the earth — the planting of the vine you did not plant, the fruit of the olive, the cleared well of water you did not dig,

3.text: “the comb of honey, the milk of the ewe, the embroidered garment with the fine wheat, and all that is necessary for them I gave: I, the LORD their God — do not grieve me as the sons of Israel grieved me and worshiped other gods.

4.text: “From those who asked of me, there is none to whom I did not give.”

1.text: “Furthermore, as David said — ‘Men ate the bread of angels’ — in the wilderness I fed them with manna; that they might worship me fittingly and in truth, I did all this for them. [Ps 78:25]

2.text: “But they did not worship me; and I disregarded them, says God who is all-powerful. They grieved me; they went in a way that was not mine.

3.text: “And I will repay them as their work. Because they have disregarded my worship, and have not stood firm in my counsel and my ordinance — as the work of their hand, I disregarded them; to the punishment of Gehenna I will bring them down.

4.text: “And they did not keep my commandment, and I will be angry with them, and shorten their days on earth.

5.text: “O king! Are you not a man who dies and decays — tomorrow worm and rotting dust?

6.text: “But today you boast and exalt yourself as a man who does not die forever.

7.text: “You are a man who today appears healthy and tomorrow dies, says God who is all-powerful.

8.text: “But if you keep my commandment and my word, I will give you to inherit a holy city with the honored kings whose dwelling is bright, whose crowns are beautiful, whose thrones are of silver and gold, who upon them are adorned and have done my will.

9.text: “In the city which is a dwelling-place prepared for those who do good works, you shall be made glad.

10.text: “But those who do wickedness shall not enter that city which the honored kings enter.

11.text: “For they have not kept my word and my ordinance, says God who is all-powerful.”

1.text: The kingdom of Media shall perish; but the kingdom of Rome shall be utterly established above the kingdom of Macedonia; and the kingdom of Nineveh shall be established above the kingdom of Persia.

2.text: And the kingdom of Ethiopia shall be established above the kingdom of Alexandria; and the kingdom of Moab shall be established above Amalek.

3.text: “Brother shall rise against brother; that they may slaughter one another — as he said, God shall do vengeance.

4.text: And he said: “Kingdom shall rise against kingdom, people against people, country against country.

5.text: “There shall be strife: war, famine, plague, earthquake, drought; for peace and love shall perish; the scourge of God shall fall upon her.

6.text: “From east to west as the visible lightning, the dreaded Day of God shall suddenly come;

7.text: “and at that time every man shall receive according to his work and the labor of his hand, according to the fruit of his work. For God himself has said: ‘On the day of judgment and the day when their foot stumbles, I will avenge myself; for the day on which they are reckoned for destruction has come.’ [Deut 32:35]

8.text: “At that time, God in eternal condemnation shall destroy those evildoers who do not walk in his law: the people of Judah and Cyprus, of Samaria and Damascus, and of Babylon;

9.text: “of the western islands, India and Nubia, Sheba and Egypt, and Ethiopia — and all who dwell in them.

10.text: “Then they shall know that I, the LORD — who rule heaven and earth, who give honor and love, who kill and save — am God.

11.text: “I am the one who brings forth the sun, and sends it to its entrance; I am the one who brings forth evil and good.

12.text: “I am the one who brings against you the heathen peoples whom you do not know — who consume the wealth you have labored for, the flock of your cows and your sheep.

13.text: “They shall lead your children captive, crushing them before your face; you cannot save them. Because the Spirit of God has not abided upon you, because you have not feared the commandment of God which you have heard — they shall consume your sweat and your freshness.

14.text: “As Nebuchadnezzar said to the prophet Daniel — ‘I see the Spirit of God upon you’ — the man on whom the Spirit of God abides knows all things.

15.text: “The man on whom the Spirit of God abides knows all; the hidden is revealed to him; he knows the revealed and the hidden. For nothing is hidden from the Spirit of God.

16.text: “But we are people who shall die tomorrow; all the work we did in hiding shall be revealed.

17.text: “As gold and silver are tested in fire — because they have not kept God’s commandment — so shall sinners be tested in the latter day.

18.text: “At that time also, all the works of the sons of Israel and of all the heathen shall be tested.”

1.text: “Because you have not judged true judgment for the orphan whose father and mother have died, God will be angry with you. Woe to you, mighty men of Israel!

2.text: “You who morning and evening go to the tavern and become drunk, who pervert justice, who do not hear the judgment of the orphan whose father and mother have died, or the judgment of the widow — who live in sin and licentiousness — woe to you!”

3.text: God says to the mighty of Israel thus: “If you have not walked in my commandment, and have not kept my word, and have not loved what I love — woe to you!

4.text: “I will bring scourge and destruction and affliction upon you; you shall perish as the moth consumes; your trace shall not be found in your districts.

5.text: “Your country shall become wilderness; everyone who saw it before shall clap his hands. ‘Was not this country full of blessing and all that is good? Has God so done to it on account of the sin of the people who dwelt in it?’” — so shall they marvel at her.

6.text: Because God has humbled her in the dust of the earth — because she has stiffened her heart; because she has exalted herself; because she has stretched out her neck — and because of the arrogance of those who dwell in her, she has become a wilderness; thistle and thorn have sprouted on her. Woe to her!

7.text: Reed and sedge she has sprouted; wilderness and desert she has become; wild beasts dwell in her.

8.text: To those who pass through her, she has become a terror. For the wrath of God has fallen upon her; on account of the arrogance of her mind and the wickedness of the people in her, she has drunk from the cup of his wrath.

1.text: Men of Macedonia, do not boast! Amalekites, do not stiffen your neck! For there is God who shall avenge himself against you.

2.text: Though you exalt yourself to heaven, you shall descend to Sheol.

3.text: Israel, in old times when they entered the land of Egypt under the kingdom of Moab and Media, [God] said: “Do not boast, for it is not fitting to contend with God.”

4.text: “You also, Ishmaelite, son of the slave-woman — why do you stretch out your neck against that which is not yours? Do you not consider that, when [she] rises to be judged in the earth, on the day of judgment God shall judge you?

5.text: “At that time you shall receive according to the work of your hand. Why do you exalt your mind? Why do you stretch out your neck? says God who rules all.

6.text: “As you have challenged those who are not your kindred — so I will challenge you; for you do what you have desired in order to do evil; therefore in the place to which I have sent you, I disregard you.

7.text: “And I will do likewise to you, says God who is all-powerful. But if you do good, and love what I love — all that you have asked, I will hear.

8.text: “If you do my will, I will do your will; I will set myself against your enemies for you; I will bless your work, your seed, and your children.

9.text: “I will bless the flock of your cows and your sheep; if you walk in my commandment, and do what I love, I will bless all on which you lay your hand, says God who is all-powerful.

10.text: “But if you do not do my will, if you do not walk in my commandment and my law — all this misery foretold before shall reach you; for I will not endure you in my commandment; you have not walked in my law; you cannot escape my wrath which always comes upon you.

11.text: “For you have not loved what I loved. Though I brought you from non-existence into existence and created you, you have neglected to praise me and worship me.

12.text: “That you might do whatever you wished, I gave you honor and lordship over those beneath you. That you might kill and save, do and undo, honor and humble, raise up and lay low — it was yours.

13.text: “And if you do the will of God and walk in his commandment, that you may be made glad with him in his lordship, that you may be a sharer with the people who have inherited the holy land — he loves you.

14.text: “For he has said: ‘If they endure me, I will give them honor and love as inheritance; in my sanctuary I will make them glad; like the sacrifice of the eucharist they shall be chosen and beloved, says God who is all-powerful.’”

15.text: Do not neglect doing good and the path of salvation, that you may cross over from death to life.

16.text: Those who do good works, however — God preserves them in all that is good, that they may be his servants like Job, whom God preserved from all evil.

17.text: Like Abraham whom he saved when he killed the kings; like Moses whom he saved from the hand of the Canaanites with whom Abraham had lived, and from the hand of Pharaoh — when they sought to make him worship the idol morning and evening, day and night, troubling his body —

18.text: but he, when they sought to draw him to their idols, endured, saying “No.”

19.text: He continued to say “No” to them; he continued to worship God who had created him. From his childhood, Abraham who had believed in him was the faithful friend of God.

20.text: Because he utterly loved God, until he died he did not neglect to worship God; until the day of his death he did not transgress his commandment; he taught his children that they should keep the commandment of God.

21.text: And as their father Abraham had done, they did not transgress the commandment of God. “I have a friend on earth whose name is Abraham,” he said to the angels — God spoke about them this way: his servants Isaac and Jacob, the children of Abraham, did not transgress God’s law.

22.text: “Abraham is my friend; Isaac is my favored one; Jacob is the beloved of my heart; in them I have been praised, says God who is all-powerful.”

23.text: And though he utterly loved the sons of Israel, they continually grieved him; and he endured them, feeding them with manna in the wilderness.

24.text: Their garments did not wear out; their feet did not become tired, for they had eaten the bread of knowledge — manna.

25.text: But their mind was always far from God; from the beginning they had been doers of wickedness; there was no hope for their salvation.

26.text: They became as a perverse bow; in their lovely conduct they did not serve God like their fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob; on their mountain and their hill they always grieved him with their idol; on the mountain, in the cave, and under the trees they ate.

27.text: They slaughtered the bull; they offered sacrifice; they rejoiced in the work of their hand; they ate of the remainder of the sacrifice; they drank the libation-portion of the drink-offering; with demons they sang and made merry.

28.text: And the demons admired all their games and songs, all their drunkenness; they fornicated beyond measure; the plunder and greed God does not love, they did.

29.text: To the idol of Canaan, to Baal; to the idol of Midian; to the idols of the Philistines, to Dagon and to Apollon; to Arṭemades and to Serapion;

30.text: to all the idols of the surrounding heathen, they offered sacrifice. They worshiped, doing all that they saw and heard the heathen do; the games and songs of the heathen, their roaring, they performed.

31.text: The people of Israel, who said “We worship God,” did so. That they might keep God’s commandments and refrain from worshiping idols —

32.text: [though God] fed them with the grain of the threshing-floor, brought them to the harvest of the land, brought near to them the honey from the comb, fed them with manna, [and gave them the Torah commandment] not to worship any god besides their fathers’ Creator as Moses had told them in the Law — yet they did not do his commandment and his law.

33.text: What they desired and sought, he did not withhold; for he is their God; he fed them what they loved.

34.text: But they did not leave off grieving God; when he gladdened them, they forgot God.

35.text: When he brought scourge upon them, they cried out to him; and from the affliction that came upon them, he saved them; again they were openly glad; they lived many years.

36.text: And immediately, as before, they returned their hearts utterly to grieve God; and he raised against them the heathen around them, that they should destroy them; afflicting them, they made them tributary.

37.text: Again, turning back, they cried swiftly to their Creator God.

38.text: And he forgave them — not on their own account, but on account of their fathers who had served God from old in their pleasing conduct, and to whom he had confirmed his oath: their fathers Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

39.text: He loved them that he might multiply their seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand of the sea — those who loved him and kept his commandment.

40.text: Those like the sand of the sea are the souls of sinners from among the sons of Israel who, at the resurrection of the dead, shall be separated and shall enter Gehenna.

41.text: But those who are called like stars shining in heaven are the souls of the righteous from among the sons of Israel. For God said to Abraham: “Look to heaven by night; count the stars of heaven if you can. So shall your righteous children shine like the stars of heaven in the kingdom of heaven.”

42.text: “Furthermore, look to the seashore and the river-shore; see what is in the sand; count it if you can. So are your children who, at the resurrection of the dead, shall descend to Gehenna.”

43.text: And Abraham believed in God; and therefore it was reckoned to him as righteousness; and his hope on earth was fulfilled — his wife Sarah, even after she had grown old, bore the son Isaac.

44.text: And again, on account of his faith, he obtains the kingdom in heaven. For he has believed:

45.text: that the dead shall rise; that those who did good works shall go to eternal life; and that those who did evil shall, at the resurrection of the dead, go to eternal punishment. But the righteous who did good works shall reign with him forever.

46.text: And the evildoers shall be judged forever. Amen. Amen.
